...so that the Salt begins to ferment with the vinegar, and this should be placed inside a <term>glazed earthenware flask <note>original: "boccia di terra vitriate"; a ceramic vessel with a glassy coating to prevent the chemicals from being absorbed into the clay.</note></term>, and its mouth should be stopped and sealed very well so that it does not breathe. For three continuous days, it should be placed in a <term>furnace at the heat of putrefaction <note>original: "calore di putrefattione"; a steady, gentle warmth, often mimicking the temperature of a dung heap, used to break down substances over time.</note></term>. Then, once finished, take the said Salt and mix it into a paste with twice its weight—or whatever amount is necessary—of <term>powdered clay <note>original: "terra creta poluerizata".</note></term> to form a dough. Form this into small balls and let them dry somewhat in a <term>stove <note>original: "stussa" (stufa); a drying chamber or heated room.</note></term>.

Then, place them inside a large <term>retort <note>original: "storta"; a glass or ceramic vessel with a long, downward-sloping neck used for distilling liquids.</note></term> that is very well <term>luted <note>original: "lutata"; sealed with a specialized paste (lute) to ensure the connection between vessels is airtight.</note></term> to its <term>receiver <note>original: "recipiente"; the vessel that collects the vapor as it condenses back into liquid.</note></term>, diligently sealing the joints. Apply a graduated fire, increasing it toward the end until the <term>volatile Salt <note>original: "Sale volatile"; a substance that vaporizes easily when heated and re-solidifies upon cooling.</note></term> of a yellowish color is seen to <term>sublimate <note>original: "solimare" (sublimare); the process of a solid turning into vapor and then back into a solid in a cooler part of the apparatus.</note></term> at the neck of the retort. Some drops of a gold color will also be seen exiting the retort. 

Once allowed to cool, take the Salt that is found around the neck of the retort and combine it with the <term>Spirit <note>original: "Spirito"; the liquid distillate collected in the receiver.</note></term> from the receiving vessel. For every four ounces of the said Spirit, take one pound of <term>decrepitated salt <note>original: "Sale decrepitato"; common salt that has been heated until it stops crackling, indicating all moisture has been removed.</note></term> and two pounds of <term>bole <note>original: "bollo" (bolo); a type of medicinal or earthy clay used as a medium for the reaction.</note></term> or clay; place this in a retort and return to distilling as described above.

<summary>This page details the fermentation of salt and vinegar, followed by a distillation process using clay "balls" to extract a yellowish volatile salt and a golden spirit.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Mercury’s role in the alchemical process, specifically how it unites with metals to return them to their "first matter." It concludes the thought from the previous page where Mercury was described as "permanent water."</meta>

# The Gift of God

it unites with them, and they no longer
separate from one another; for this
reason they call it the permanent water <note>original: "bleibendig Wasser," a German translation of the Latin "aqua permanens."</note>.
They also call it *aqua vitae* <note>original: "aquam vitæ," meaning "water of life."</note>, that is
the living water. For when
Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius." In alchemy, Mercury is often personified or treated as the fundamental "spirit" of all metals.</note> is added to the metals,
he brings them back into their first essence—
that is, into Mercury, which then
never stands still or rests,
but moves at all times
and is alive. Therefore,
they call Mercury *aqua vitae*, the
living water, and give many more
names to Mercury because
of its properties, which
I will omit for the sake of brevity.
For in this way, one confirms the
saying of the master of nature,
Aristotle: *Let the practitioners of alchemy know that the species of metals cannot be changed* <note>original Latin: "Sciant Artifices Alchymiæ species permutari non posse." This famous quote, actually from a medieval text attributed to Aristotle, was a warning that alchemists cannot simply change the outward appearance of a metal; they must decompose it entirely to its "prime matter" before a true transformation can occur.</note>. This is as much
as to say: the practitioners of alchemy
should know that they can never
transform the essence of metals—
and that is true—unless
they are first transformed

<header>HET VYFDE BOECK.</header>

Gelyck teelt zijns gelijck. zoo zeght men oock met reden :
Hy is, als waer hy uit zijn aengezicht gesneden,
Den vader gansch gelijck. zoo ziet men een manier,
Een' aert in plaet, en print; een' ommetreck, een' zwier.
Godt ziet dien eenigen, en eigen uitverkoren,
Natuurlijcken Zoon, en eeuwigh eerstgeboren,
En noemt hem zijnen Zoon, een' Zoon, die hem behaeght,
En daer de vaderschap met recht haer' naem af draeght,
Gelijck de zoonschap neemt haer' oirsprong van den Vader:
Wat straelden deze beide, onscheibaer hecht te gader
Verknocht, toch anders dan den Geest der liefde, een' gloet
Des Vaders, en des Zoons, van wederzy gevoedt?
Dus openbaerden zich, in een' alom gespreiden,
En 't eenigh wezen, dry al teffens ongescheiden,
Doch onderscheiden, elck door dry byzonderheên.
Geen zonderlingheit deelt nochtans dees dry van een.
Een wezen deelt zich mede aen dry byzonderheden.
De dry, by zich bestaende, in geen vermenging treden,
Maer blijven op zich zelve, en enckel in der daet,
Naerdien d'eenwezenheit der dry op 't wezen staet,
En by gemeenschap van het wezen: dat blijft enckel:
Dat spatte noit van zich, gelijck een vonck, een sprenckel
Van eene vlamme spat. hier is een vlam, een licht,
Een puure louterheit, gesloten vast en dicht;
Een loutre eenvouwigkeit, een Godtheit, puur en simpel;
Een effen aenschijn, dat geen kreucken zet noch rimpel.
Al Godt, en Godtheit; een gelijckheit in dry een,
En een in dry: naerdien d'eenwezenheit hier geen
Dryvuldigheit ontkent, maer aenhoudt die te kroonen
Door ongescheidenheit, al hoort men dry persoonen.
Maer eer wy verder gaen omzweven in dien ring
Der Godtheit; luister eerst hoe Godts bespiegeling,
En beelt, en 't straelen van de liefde dezer beiden
Noit iemant buiten Godt, het eenigh wezen, leidden.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of God's "internal work" described on page 194. Having established that God's essence and His activity are co-eternal, the author now focuses on the generation of the Son and the procession of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that these distinctions do not divide the single divine essence.</meta>

# THE FIFTH BOOK.

Like begets like; so it is said with reason:
He is, as if cut from his own face <note>A Dutch idiom meaning he is the "spitting image" or a perfect likeness.</note>,
Entirely like the Father. Thus one sees a manner,
A nature in image and print; a contour, a certain grace.
God beholds that only, and His own chosen,
Natural Son, and eternally firstborn,
And calls him His Son, a Son who pleases Him,
And from whom the name of fatherhood rightfully derives,
Just as sonship takes its origin from the Father:
What did these two—inseparably bound and fastened
Together—radiate, if not the Spirit of love, a glow
Of the Father and the Son, nourished by both?
Thus there revealed themselves, in a widely spread
And single essence, three all at once undivided,
Yet distinct, each by three particularities.
No singularity, however, divides these three from one another.
One essence shares itself among three particularities.
The three, existing by themselves, enter into no mingling <note>This refers to the theological rejection of "Modalism," the idea that the three Persons of the Trinity are just different "modes" or roles of one person rather than distinct subsistent relations.</note>,
But remain in themselves, and are simple in deed,
Since the <term>consubstantiality<gloss>The doctrine that the Father, Son, and Spirit are "of one substance" or essence (Greek: homoousios).</gloss></term> of the three rests upon the essence,
And by the sharing of the essence: that remains simple:
It never sparks away from itself, like a spark, a sprinkle
Spattering from a flame. Here is a flame, a light,
A pure clarity, closed firm and tight;
A pure simplicity, a <term>Godhead<gloss>The essential nature or "being" of God, as opposed to the individual "Persons."</gloss></term>, pure and simple;
A smooth countenance that shows no creases or wrinkles.
All God, and Godhead; an equality in three-in-one,
And one in three: since the <term>essential unity<gloss>The state of being one in essence or nature.</gloss></term> here denies no
Trinity, but continues to crown it
Through indivisibility, even though one hears of three persons.
But before we wander further in that ring
Of the Godhead; listen first to how God’s contemplation,
And image, and the radiance of the love of these two
Never led anyone outside of God, the unique Being.

<sig>Bb 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: God's</meta>

<summary>This page explains the Trinity using metaphors of light and parental likeness, arguing that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct "Persons" who nonetheless share a single, indivisible, and simple essence.</summary>
<keywords>Trinity, Father and Son, Holy Spirit, consubstantiality, divine essence, simplicity of God, Godhead, theological poetry</keywords>

The Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Ming Dynasty: Luo Wood Mountain is located eighty miles northeast of the seat of Yongchang Military and Civilian Prefecture. It sits on the west bank of the Lancang River. It is over one thousand <term>ren</term> <gloss>a measurement of approximately seven to eight feet</gloss> high and extends more than forty miles. Stones frequently fly down from the summit; those passing by must hurry.

Luo Cliff <note>Luo Yan</note>
The Commentary on the Water Classic: The Ying River originates in Lengdao County, Yingyang, and flows south of the mountains, then west, passing beneath the Jiuyi Mountains. It sits firmly across the wilderness of Cangwu, its peaks standing out elegantly among several prefectures. The Luo Cliffs rise up in nine places, each leading to a stream. The peaks and ravines lean against the rugged terrain; though the ridges are distinct, they share the same imposing momentum. Travelers find the layout confusing, which is why it is called Jiuyi <gloss>Nine Uncertainties</gloss> Mountain.

Luo Grove <note>Luo Cong</note>
The Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Ming Dynasty: Luo Grove Rock is located sixty miles southwest of the seat of Xunzhou Prefecture. The cliff is bright and spacious, capable of holding two or three hundred people. Inside, there is a Hall of the Three Religions. To the east and west are two caves, Bixu <gloss>Jade Void</gloss> and Lingyuan <gloss>Spiritual Source</gloss>. It is truly a scenic landmark of Xunzhou. Every year on the Double Ninth Festival, the people of the prefecture climb to this high point.

A monk asked: When people of the world are sick, the King of Medicine heals them. When the King of Medicine is sick, who heals him?
The Master extended his hand and said: Feel my pulse and see.
The monk said: I do not understand.
The Master said: Mount Sumeru is used as medicine in vain; the four seas are uselessly turned into broth.
A monk asked: The "One Path Upward" is not transmitted by a thousand sages. Does the Reverend still transmit it?
The Master said: An iron ball is stuffed into the mouth; it is rare to find someone who can swallow it.
A monk asked: What is the great meaning of the Buddha Dharma?
The Master said: Facing the fire when the snow is cold; leaning toward the sun when the day is warm.
A monk asked: Who is the "Guest among Guests"?
The Master said: A profligate son with no household plan, drifting like a tumbleweed without knowing it.
The monk asked: Who is the "Master among Guests"?
The Master said: A pearl curtain hanging over a thatched door.
The monk asked: Who is the "Guest among Masters"?
The Master said: Sitting on a grass mat inside a dragon palace.
The monk asked: Who is the "Master among Masters"?

Volume 36, Part 1

# Frivolous Words <note>original: 輕薄語 "qingbo yu"; refers to shallow or flippant speech</note>
According to Zu Yong. From Helan Guang and Zheng She in recent times. Zu Yong’s <term>zi</term> <gloss>courtesy name</gloss> was Xiao Xin. This term appears in fables by Ji Yu and in cryptic riddles.

# Rapid Words <note>original: 速語 "su yu"</note>
The Miscellaneous Morsels from Youyang <note>a Tang dynasty collection of legends and anecdotes</note> states that the shrike is traditionally said to be the transformation of Bo Qi. If one takes the branch the bird has trodden upon and uses it as a switch to whip a small child, it can make the child speak quickly.

# Patched Words <note>original: 臏語 "bin yu"; likely referring to supplementary or fragmented speech</note>
The Talk Garden of Yang Wengong <note>Yang Yi, a Song dynasty scholar</note> records hearing this at music bureau banquets.

# Vacuous Words <note>original: 謾語 "man yu"; refers to empty or exaggerated speech lacking substance</note>
The Later Records of Things Heard and Seen notes that Han Zhongxian's <note>Han Qi, a prominent Song statesman</note> great-grandfather, Wei Gu, held no official rank. When Han Qi became noble, his ancestor was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian. However, there was nothing of note to record about him. When Li Bangzhi composed the spirit-way stele <note>a commemorative funeral monument</note>, he wrote over three hundred words without a single factual word about the man's life. People of that generation considered this an exceptionally difficult feat of writing.

# Deceptive Words <note>original: 謾語 "man yu"; here used in the context of lying</note>
The Later Records of Things Heard and Seen reports: I saw a letter personally written by Sima Guang. When Guang was five or six years old, he was playing with green walnuts. His older sister wanted to peel the skin for him but could not. After she left, a maid used hot water to remove the skin. When the sister returned and asked, Guang said, "I peeled it myself." His father happened to see this and scolded him, saying, "How dare this boy tell lies?" From then on, Sima Guang never dared to speak deceptively.

# Invented Words <note>original: 造語 "zao yu"</note>
The New Talks While Catching Lice <note>a work of literary criticism by Mai Yuanshou</note> states: One who can establish an original idea may not necessarily be able to express it well; one who can use fine language may not necessarily avoid vulgarity in their inventions.

# Formulaic Words <note>original: 詞語 "ci yu"</note>
The Brush Records of the Eastern Pavilion states: Tao Gu’s literary style was the best of his time. When someone recommended him, Emperor Taizhu laughed and said, "I have heard that the Hanlin scholars drafting edicts all just take old templates from predecessors and change the names. This is what the common folk call 'painting a gourd according to the model.'"

# Extracted Words <note>original: 摘語 "zhai yu"</note>
The Sea of Jade <note>an encyclopedia by Wang Yinglin</note> records: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang produced the Book of the Golden Mirror and commanded Linghu Tao, saying, "This was written by Emperor Taizong. Summarize its essential points for me." Linghu Tao extracted these words: "At the peak of order, the unworthy were never employed; at the peak of chaos, the virtuous were never employed."

# Judgment Words <note>original: 判語 "pan yu"</note>
The Wild Records of Xiangshan states: Whenever Zhang Zhongding <note>Zhang Yong, a Northern Song official</note> decided a legal case, he would always write a judgment to explain it to the people. The people of Shu <note>Sichuan</note> carved these onto woodblocks and called them the Collection for Admonishing the People.

# Waking Words <note>original: 寤語 "wu yu"</note>
Wang Bao's Nine Regrets states: I drift in a half-sleep, alas; who is there to pity me, with whom can I walk? In the Rhapsody by Xie Tiao: Relying on private banquets to wander and play, occasionally waking to roam at leisure. In the poetry of Zheng Gu...

<summary>This page catalogs various classifications of "words" or speech styles in Chinese literature, citing historical anecdotes from the Tang and Song dynasties to illustrate frivolous, deceptive, and formulaic language.</summary>
<keywords>Sima Guang, Han Qi, Tao Gu, linguistics, Chinese historiography, Tang Dynasty, Song Dynasty, ethics of speech</keywords>

He Wu’s Recommendation <note>The phrase refers to a specific political act or recommendation made by the Han official He Wu.</note>
The Book of Han, Biographies of He Wu, Wang Jia, and Shi Dan, in the Commentary: <note>The text evaluates the political stances of these three officials.</note> The recommendations of He Wu, the disputes of Wang Jia, and the debates of Shi Dan were all tested by the subsequent outcomes of fortune or disaster. The note states: He Wu recommended Gongsun Lu for the position of Grand Marshal; Wang Jia disputed the increase of Dong Xian's fiefdom; and Shi Dan debated against the proposal that the Ding family <note>the family of Emperor Ai's mother</note> should be granted imperial titles.

Recommendation of the Five Prefectures
The Book of Han, Biography of 段會宗 <term>Duan Huizong</term>: During the Jingning era, while Duan Huizong was serving as the Magistrate of Duling, he was recommended by the Five Prefectures to serve as the Protector General of the Western Regions and Cavalry Commandant. The Western Regions respected his authority and trustworthiness.

Recommendation of the Filial and Incorrupt <note>original: <term>Xiaolian</term>; the standard path for civil service entry in the Han Dynasty.</note>
The Book of Later Han, Annals of Emperor He: In the seventh year of the Yongyuan era, an imperial edict stated: Following the old statutes, we use the recommendation of the Filial and Incorrupt to find suitable men. Let the officials in charge carefully select thirty gentlemen-officers who are broad-minded, strategic, and capable of governing a city. Also, in the Biography of Zhou Pan: Pan lived in poverty to support his mother, and his meager means were insufficient. Once, while reciting the final chapter of the Ru Fen poem from the Book of Songs, he sighed with deep emotion. He then untied his leather belt <note>a sign of retiring from private life</note> and accepted the recommendation of the Filial and Incorrupt.

Recommendation of Ascending Sages
The Book of Later Han, Biography of Huang Qiong, in the Commentary: Prepared with dark and crimson silks and jade presents, the Emperor sought to recruit Fan Ying of Nanyang. The Son of Heaven descended from his sleeping quarters, established an altar and seating, and the Secretary conducted the introduction to ask about successes and failures. Urgently seeking the recommendation of ascending sages, the Emperor humbled himself through these rites. Consequently, recluses and simple scholars forgot their restrictive rituals, brushed off their caps, adjusted their coarse clothing, and eagerly looked toward the recruitment of the imperial carriage.

Han Jue’s Recommendation <note>A reference to the selfless recommendation style of Han Jue from the Spring and Autumn period.</note>
The Book of Later Han, Biography of Zuo Xiong: Xiong recommended Zhou Ju to be a Secretary. He also recommended Feng Zhi, but Zhi was later convicted of bribery. Zhou Ju used this to impeach and report Xiong. Xiong said happily: I once served Feng Zhi's father and am a friend of Zhi; now that Xuanguang <note>Zhou Ju’s courtesy name</note> reports me for this, it is truly a recommendation in the spirit of Han Jue. Because of this, the whole world admired him.

The Vermilion Banner Recommendation
The Book of Later Han, Narrative Biographies: The Divine Mother announced the omen, and the vermilion banner was then raised.

Tang Yin’s Recommendation <note>Or "The Recommendation of Yin," referring to the Tang family context.</note>
The Book of Later Han, Biography of Ban Gu: In the early Yong平 <term>Yongping</term> era, Cang, the Prince of Dongping, served as General of the Agile Cavalry and assisted in government because of his status as a close relative. He opened the Eastern Gate to welcome heroes. At that time, Ban Gu had just reached his twentieth year <note>original: <term>ruoguan</term></note>. He submitted a memorandum to persuade Cang, saying: I have observed that your command office has newly opened and is expanding...

Of Red and White Horses <note>original: "赭白馬賦"</note>, Preface: The clothing and carriages follow his will, <note>the movements are</note> harmonious and measured. Shen Yue, Preface to Buddhist Records <note>original: "佛記序"</note>: Arising and ceasing, returning and circling, without ceasing. Zhang Shuai, Poetic Exposition on Dancing Horses <note>original: "舞馬賦"</note>: How could they merely wear black <note>stable clothes</note> and be raised in peace, or proceed to the carriage to <unclear>two characters</unclear>? Du Fu, Poetic Exposition: The steps of Yao and the strides of Shun, the <unclear>one character</unclear> of Yu and the <unclear>one character</unclear> of Tang. Also a poem: The gentleman exerts himself in a winding path, while the petty man is exhausted by **sudden racing** <note>original: "馳驟"</note>. Han Yu, Poem on the Southern Mountains: Some are fluttering like <unclear>one character</unclear>, some floating like boats, some swift as if **racing** <note>original: "快驟"</note>.

Added: **Arrow-like speed** <note>original: "矢驟"</note>.
Book of Song, Biography of Zhang Xingshi: Liu Hu personally led twenty-six armies of water and land forces to attack at dawn. The officers and soldiers wanted to meet the attack, but Xingshi forbade them, saying: "The rebels are still far away and their spirit is high; once they have **raced** <note>original: "力驟"</note> until their strength is spent, their vigor will easily decline. This is how Cao Gui defeated the State of Qi."

**Rain-like speed** <note>original: "雨驟"</note>.
History of the Southern Dynasties, Biography of Yu Daomin: His biological mother was adrift in Jiaozhou while Daomin was still in **swaddling clothes** <note>original: "襁褓"</note>. When he grew up and learned of this, he braved dangers to go to Jiaozhou to seek his mother. He once entered a village at **sunset** <note>original: "日暮"</note> and stayed with a family. He saw an old woman returning from outside carrying firewood, and Daomin's heart was moved. Upon inquiring, he found it was his mother. Rare Names of Various Things, Commentary: The Stele of the Altar for Feng and Shan Sacrifices says: Those who hasten to the Phoenix Pavilion gather like mist; those who cry at the Dragon Gate <note>arrive with</note> **rain-like speed** <note>original: "雨驟"</note>. Wang Bo, Poetic Exposition: The wind startles <unclear>one character</unclear>, the smoke returns, the lightning flashes, and the **rain falls fast** <note>original: "雨驟"</note>. Lü Lingze, Poetic Exposition: The rivers flow <unclear>one character</unclear>, the **rain falls fast** <note>original: "雨驟"</note>.

**Too sudden** <note>original: "太驟"</note>.
History of the Song, Biography of Wu Xi: In the fifth year of Chunxi, he exchanged his position for the rank of Gentleman of Military Virtue and was appointed as a Middle Commander. The Palace Secretariat remarked that his **promotion was too sudden** <note>original: "改武冀郎太驟"</note>. 

**Galloping away** <note>original: "決驟"</note>.
Carriages and horses come and go here, rising like the wind and shaking like clouds; Emperors and Kings travel from here. Zhuangzi: Mao Qiang and Lady Ji are what men consider beautiful, but if fish see them, they **dive deep** <note>original: "深入"</note>; if birds see them, they fly high; if deer see them, they **gallop away** <note>original: "決驟"</note>. Of these four, which one knows the true beauty of the world? Xiao Xin, Poetic Exposition on the White Deer: Suddenly looking back to leap or lean, then **galloping away** <note>original: "決驟"</note> to circle around. Su Shi, Song of the Return: The wild horses of the field are in a chaotic **gallop** <note>original: "決驟"</note>, I am fortunate that my head is not yet bridled.

**Sudden snow** <note>original: "雪驟"</note>.
<note>Note: The text repeats "Sudden snow" followed by "shuo" (explained/said) at the bottom.</note>

<meta>continues from previous page: ...not driving. The</meta> <term>art of the cartwright</term> <gloss>the skill of wheel-making</gloss> is not merely about carving and paring. <note>From the commentary on the Huainanzi</note> The <term>art of the cartwright</term> values the completion of the carriage so it can carry loads, not just the carving and paring into a polished surface.

### The Skill of Gong Chui
<note>Gong Chui was a legendary master craftsman or artisan from the time of the Yellow Emperor.</note>
The Yinwenzi states: One values the <term>skill of Gong Chui</term> not because of his individual ingenuity, but because his skill can be shared and used by everyone. The <term>Yuanbao Jing</term> <gloss>Classic of the Primal Hidden</gloss> says: To discuss principles while abandoning numbers is like making music while discarding the tones, or making vessels while throwing away the compass and square. Even with the hearing of Master Kuang <note>a legendary music master</消失> or the <term>skill of Gong Chui</term>, how could one avoid making mistakes?

### The Skill of Ou Ye
</note><note>Ou Yezi was a famous swordsmith of the Spring and Autumn period.</note>
The Huainanzi says: Obtaining ten sharp swords is not as good as obtaining the <term>skill of Ou Ye</term>; obtaining a hundred galloping horses is not as good as mastering the methods of Bo Le <note>a legendary judge of horses</note>.

### The Skill of Artisans
The Huainanzi says: Farmers speak with farmers about strength; scholars speak with scholars about conduct; artisans speak with <term>artisans about skill</term>; merchants speak with merchants about numbers.

### The Skill of Needlework
The Yantielun <gloss>Discourses on Salt and Iron</gloss> says: When Grand Duke Wang was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, he cleared the weeds and lived there. The land was poor and the population sparse, so he opened up the trade of salt and silk and pushed the <term>skill of needlework</term> <note>women's manual labor, specifically textile arts</note> to the limit. Wealth accumulated and goods multiplied, and for generations, it remained a powerful state. The Fayuan Zhulin <gloss>Forest of Gems in the Garden of the Law</gloss> says: When a Bodhisattva is in the mother’s womb, if the mother possesses thirty-two auspicious signs, she can endure it. Furthermore, that mother possesses the ultimate <term>skill of needlework</term>.

### The Skill of the Five Colors
The Lunheng states: Apply the <term>skill of the five colors</term> <note>embroidery using various colored threads</note> to decorate the tip of a needle.

### The Skill of Common Doctors
The Lunheng says: For minor illnesses, <term>common doctors are all skilled</term>; but for severe and acute illnesses, only a doctor like Bian Que is truly excellent.

### The Skill of the Clumsy Woman
The Lunheng says: In the state of Qi, embroidery is a common custom, and there is no woman who cannot do it. In the local villages, silk weaving is common, and even a <term>clumsy woman possesses the skill</term>. Because they see it every day and do it every day, their hands become familiar with it. Also, the Lingbiao Luyi <gloss>Strange Records from the Southern Lands</gloss> notes: The "pounding hall" uses a solid log stripped to make a trough. On both sides of the trough, about ten poles are arranged. Men and women stand alternately to pound the rice and grain. The sound of the pounding on the wooden trough has a rhythmic beat that can be heard for several miles. Even the skill of Si Hui <note>a legendary artisan</note> or the melancholy sound of autumn laundry-pounding blocks cannot compare to its clear and resonant tone.

### The Skill of the Lu Scholar
Liu Xie's Xinlun <gloss>New Discussions</gloss> says: The cloud-ladder floats like smoke through the <term>skill of the Lu scholar</term> <note>referring to Lu Ban, the patron god of Chinese builders</note>.

### Minute Skill
<note>Refers to extremely fine or delicate craftsmanship.</note>
The <term>minute skill</term>... <note>text cuts off</note> heart...

<summary>This page compiles literary and philosophical references to various forms of skill and craftsmanship, ranging from legendary artisans like Gong Chui and Lu Ban to the everyday textile skills of women.</summary>

<note>The following entries continue the categorization of "Zhang" </note><note>the Zhang River</note> combined with other characters to form geographic and literary terms.

<column-break/>
In the fourth year of the Kaiyuan era <note>716 CE</note>, the administrative seat was moved to Li'aochuan. The county had the Sanlong Stream and the Longyan <term>Zhangpu</term> <gloss>The Zhang River Plain/County</gloss>. In the History of the Song Dynasty, in the Biography of Chuan Bocheng, it is noted that when he went to govern Zhangzhou, he built a bridge of thirty-five sections from the south gate of the commandery to <term>Zhangpu</term> <gloss>The Zhang River Plain</gloss>, covering a distance of one thousand two hundred <term>zhang</term> <gloss>a unit of length approximately 3.3 meters</gloss>. In the Records of the Yuanhe Era, it is stated that Quanzhou managed three counties: <term>Zhangpu</term> <gloss>The Zhang River Plain</gloss> was established during the Chuigong era <note>685–688 CE</note> by partitioning the southern border of Longxi. Furthermore, in Wang Can's Rhapsody on the Imperial Hunt: Crossing the <term>Zhangshui</term> <gloss>Zhang River</gloss> to form a horizontal battle array, leaning against the purple paths and marching together. In Lu Sidao's poem: Having just set out from the clear <term>Zhangshui</term> <gloss>Zhang River</gloss>, the spring grass is growing lush and green. In Zheng Yin's Song of the Bronze Bird Terrace: The sun sets over the <term>Zhangshui</term> <gloss>Zhang River</gloss> as the wind rises, the Ye Terrace grows cold. In Bai Juyi's poem: Changsha was empty for Jia Yi's <term>Zhangshui</term> <gloss>Zhang River</gloss>, <column-break/> while <term>Zhangshui</term> <gloss>Zhang River</gloss> saw Liu Zhen lying ill.

# Zhang
# Qi

In the General Interpretation of Geography: The Hebei Circuit covers the borders of the ancient You and Ji Provinces. It currently comprises twenty-five prefectures. Its great rivers include the waters of the <term>Zhangqi</term> <gloss>Zhang and Qi Rivers</gloss> and the Hutuo River.

# Zhang Huai

In the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Ming Dynasty: <term>Zhanghuai</term> <gloss>The Zhang and Huai Rivers/Locality</gloss> is located sixty <term>li</term> <gloss>Chinese miles</gloss> south of Nanling County in Ningguo Prefecture. Its source emerges from Mount Lü; reaching the eastern stream of the county, it merges with the waters of Zhonggang and Xigang and flows into the Lesser Huai River. Reaching Shipao, it flows west out of Lugang and reaches the Great Yangtze River.

In Ruan Ji's Treatise on Music: Between the Yangtze and the Huai, the people are fond of destruction; between the <term>Zhangru</term> <gloss>Zhang and Ru Rivers</gloss>, the people are fond of fleeing.

གི་ཁ་འབར་མ་བཞུགས་སོ། །རང་རང་གིས་རྐང་པའི་རྩ་བཞག་འཁྱིལ་པའི་ནང་ན ། རང་བྱུང་གི་ཨ་བ་གླང་མགོ་ཅན་བཞུགས་སོ། །རང་རང་ག་ཙིཏྟའི་དཀྱིལ་ན་ཞི་བའི་
ལྷ་ཚོགས་བཞུགས་ཚུལ་བསྟན་པའི་ལེའུ་སྟེ་གཉིས་པའོ།། །།ཀྱེ་གསང་བའི་བདག་པོ ། ཁྲོ་བོའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཐམས་ཅད་རང་རང་གི་ཀླད་པ་དུང་
ཁང་གཞལ་ཡས་ཁང་ན ། སྡོང་པོ་ལས་མེ་ཏོག་རྒྱས་པ་ལྟར་དུ་བཞུགས་སོ། །བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དཔལ་བཛྲ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་སྐུ་མདོག་མཐིང་ནག །དབུ་གསུམ་པ །
ཞལ་གཡས་དཀར་བ ། གཡོན་དམར་བ ། དབུས་མཐིང་ནག་ལ ། ཞབས་བཞི་གྱད་ཀྱི་དོར་སྟབས་སུ་བཞུགས་པ ། ཕྱག་དྲུག་པ ། གཡས་ཀྱི་དང་པོ་ན་རྡོ་རྗེ་འབར་
བ་དང་ ། བར་མ་ན་རལ་གྲི་བསྣམས་པ ། ཐ་མ་ན་བནྡྷ་དང་དགྲ་སྟ་བསྣམས་པ ། གཡོན་གྱི་དང་པོ་ན་དྲིལ་བུ་དང་ ། བར་པ་ན་བནྡྷ་དམར་གྱིས་བཀང་བ ། ཐ་མ་ན་ཐོང་
གཤོལ་བསྣམས་པ ། ཡུམ་བཛྲ་ཀྲོ་དྷི་མ་ཡབ་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ལ་འཁྲིལ་བ ། མགུལ་ནས་འཁྱུད་པ ། ཞལ་དུ་སྟོབ་པ ། རང་གི་ཀླད་པ་དུང་ཁང་གི་དཀྱིལ་ན་བཞུགས་སོ། །བཅོམ
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། །དཀར་བ ། གཡོན་དམར་བ ། དབུས་དམར་ནག་ལ ། ཞབས་བཞི་གྱད་ཀྱི་དོར་སྟབས་སུ་བཞུགས་སོ། །ཕྱག་དྲུག་པ ། གཡས་ཀྱི་དང་པོ་ན་པདྨ །
བར་པ་ན་ཁ་ཊྭཱཾ་ག ། ཐ་མ་ན་དབྱུག་ཏོ་བསྣམས་པ ། གཡོན་དང་པོ་དྲིལ་བུ ། བར་མ་ན་བན་དྷ་དམར་གྱིས་བཀང་བ ། ཐ་མ་ན་རྗེའུ་ཆུང་བསྣམས་པ ། ཡུམ་པདྨ་ཀྲོ་དྷི་མ་
ཡབ་ལ་འཁྲིལ་བ ། མགུལ་ནས་འཁྱུད་པ ། ཞལ་དུ་སྟོབ་པ ། གཡས་པ་རཀྟ་སྒྲེང་བ ། རང་གི་ཀླད་པ་དུང་ཁང་གི་ནུབ་ན་བཞུགས་སོ། །བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དཔལ་ཀརྨ་ཧེ་
རུ་ཀ་སྐུ་མདོག་ལྗང་ནག ། དབུ་གསུམ་པ ། ཞལ་གཡས་དཀར་བ ། གཡོན་དམར་བ། དབུས་ལྗང་ནག ཞབས་བཞི་གྱད་ཀྱི་དོར་སྟགས་སུ་བཞུགས་པ ། ཕྱག་དྲུག་པ །
གཡས་ཀྱི་དང་པོ་ན་རལ་གྲི ། བར་པ་ན་ཁ་ཊྭཱཾ་ག ཐ་མ་ན་དབྱུག་ཏོ ། གཡོན་གྱི་དང་པོ་ན་དྲིལ་བུ ། བར་པ་ན་བནྡྷ་དམར་གྱིས་བཀང་བ ། མཐའ་མ་ན་ཐོང་གཤོལ་བསྣམས་
པ ། ཡུམ་ཀརྨ་ཀྲོ་དྷི་ཤྭ་རི་མ་ཡབ་ལ་འཁྲིལ་བ ། མགུལ་བས་འཁྱུད་པ ། ཞལ་དུ་སྟོང་པ ། ཁུ་ཚུར་འཆང་བ ། རང་རང་གི་ཀླད་པ་དུང་ཁང་གཞལ་ཡས་ཁང་གི་བྱང་
ན་བཞུགས་སོ། །ཀྱེ་གསང་བའི་བདག་པོ ། ཤར་ན་ཀེའུ་རི་མ་དཀར་མོ ། ཕྱག་གཡས་ན་ཞིང་དབྱུག་ཐོགས་པ ། གཡོན་པ་ན་བནྡྷ་དམར་གྱིས་དཀར་བ་བསྣམས་པ །

In the center of the emanation wheel <note>the navel chakra</note> at the navel, the self-arising Buddha Extremely Firm resides. In the secret place that generates bliss <note>the sexual center</note> of each being, the self-arising Kha-bar-ma <gloss>the Blazing-Mouthed One</gloss> resides. Within the coiled station of the channels at the soles of each being's feet, the self-arising ox-headed Ava resides. This is the second chapter, showing how the assembly of peaceful deities resides in the center of the heart of each being.

O Lord of Secrets, all the wrathful Buddhas reside within the celestial palace of the skull-mansion of the brain, like flowers blooming from a trunk. The Blessed Lord, the Glorious Vajra Heruka, has a dark blue body, three heads—the right is white, the left is red, and the center is dark blue—and four legs standing in the heroic posture of a giant. He has six arms: the first right hand holds a blazing vajra, the middle one a sword, and the last a skull-cup and a battle-axe. The first left hand holds a bell, the middle one a skull-cup filled with red blood, and the last a plowshare. The consort Vajra Kroshvari clings to the body of the Father, embracing his neck and offering to his mouth. He resides in the center of the skull-mansion of your own brain. The Blessed...

<leaf-break/>

...white, the left is red, and the center is dark red-black, standing with four legs in the heroic posture. He has six arms: the first right holds a lotus, the middle a <term>khatvanga</term> <gloss>trident-staff</gloss>, and the last a club. The first left holds a bell, the middle a skull-cup filled with red blood, and the last a small knife. The consort Padma Krodhishvari clings to the Father, embracing his neck, offering to his mouth, and holding a vessel of blood in her right hand. He resides in the west of the skull-mansion of your own brain. The Blessed Lord, the Glorious Karma Heruka, has a dark green body and three heads: the right is white, the left is red, and the center is dark green. He stands with four legs in the heroic posture. He has six arms: the first right holds a sword, the middle a <term>khatvanga</term>, and the last a club. The first left holds a bell, the middle a skull-cup filled with red blood, and the last a plowshare. The consort Karma Krodhishvari clings to the Father, embracing his neck, offering to his mouth, and holding her fists. They reside in the north of the celestial palace of the skull-mansion of each brain. O Lord of Secrets, in the east is white Gauri, holding a human-skin club in her right hand and a skull-cup filled with red blood in her left.

བདེ་བར་འགྱུར ། མགོན་མེད་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མགོན་དུ་འགྱུར་རོ། ། ངས་ཀྱང་གནང་ཞིང་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ངོ་། ། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། དེ་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་
སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་པོས་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་དབང་ཕྱུག་གི་མ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གཟུངས་ཀྱི་རིག་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོའི་གསང་སྔགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་འདི་དག་སྨྲས་སོ། ། དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། །
བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་འོད་དཔག་མེད་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་ལྡན་པ་འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་དབང་དུ་ཕྱུག་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་
ལོ། ། དེ་དག་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ནས། འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིག་དབང་ཕྱུག་གི་ཡུམ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གཟུངས་རིག་སྔགས་ཆེན་མོའི་གསངས་སྔགས་ཀྱི་གཞི་འདི་དག་བརྗོད་པར་བྱའོ། ། བདག་ལ་རིག་པ་འདི་གྲུབ་
པར་གྱུར་ཅིག ། ཏདྱ་ཐཱ། ཨི་ལི་མི་ལི། ཙི་ལི་མི་ལི། ཀུ་ཤུ་ལེ། ཀུ་ཤུ་ལེ་སི་རི། སི་སི་རི། བི་སི་རི། བི་རཱ་ཡཱུ། གོ་རི། གརྦྷ་རི། དྲཱ་མི་རི། མ་ཏ་དྠི། པཱུཀྐ་སི། ཀཱཉྩ་ཡ།
མཱ་ལ་ཙནྡ་ལཱི། ཙིནྡུ་དྷུ་དྷུ་མ་ལི་ནི། ཙི་ལི་མི་ལི། བྲྀ་ཧྞ་སོ་སྱ་དེ་དྭ་ནི། ཀུ་ཤུ་ཙནྡྲ་མུ་ཁེ། ལཱ་བྷུ་མཱ་ན་ཡ་ཏི། ཨཱརྱ་ད་ཀྲི་ཎ་བྷུ་ཛེ། སརྦ་བིདྭཱ་ནཱ་མ། པྲ་སཱ་དྷ་ནི། སརྦ་བིདྭཱ་ནཱ་མ།
བཀླགས་པས་གྲུབ་པའི་གཟུངས་འདིའི་ཆོ་ག་ནི་འདི་ཡིན་ཏེ། ཐོས་མ་ཐ་ག་ཏུ་ལས་ཀྱི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱང་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། ། འཇིགས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་བསྲུང་ངོ་། ། དུས་གསུམ་དུ་བཟླས་པ་བྱས་ན་ཞག་བདུན་གྱིས་
<leaf-break/>
༄༅། ། ཕྱག་བཞི་པ། དང་པོ་གཉིས་ཐལ་མོ་སྦྱར་བ། གཡས་འོག་མ་ན་བགྲང་ཕྲེང་མུ་ཏིག་དཀར་པོ། གཡོན་འོག་མ་ན་པདྨ་དཀར་པོ་བསྣམས་པ། སྐུ་མདོག་དཀར་པོ་ཞབས་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐྱིལ་ཀྲུང་
བཅས་པ་རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་རྒྱན་སྣ་ཚོགས་དང་། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་དབུ་རྒྱན་གྱིས་མཛེས་པ། ཨ་ལྷ་མོ་དྲུག་མ་དང་། ཨ་བ་ནོར་གུ་རིན་པོ་ཆེས་བརྟེན་པ། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དང་། སེམས་མ་རབ་ཏུ་མང་པོས་བསྐོར་ཏེ་འདི་སྐད་དོ། །
ཅེས་གསུངས་སོ། ། རིགས་ཀྱི་བུའམ། རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་མོས་སྔགས་འདི་ལན་ཅིག་ཙམ་བརྗོད་དམ་དྲན་ཞིང་ཡིད་ལ་བྱས་སམ། བྲིས་ནས་ལུས་ལ་བཅངས་སམ། མོས་ཤིང་གུས་པར་བྱས་ན་མཚམས་མེད་པ་ལྔ་དང་། དེ་
དང་ཉེ་བའི་སྡིག་པའི་ལས་ཐམས་ཅད་འབྱང་ཞིང་ངན་སོང་གསུམ་དང་། མི་ཁོམ་པ་བརྒྱད་དང་། སྡུག་བསྔལ་དང་བཅས་པ་མར་མི་སྐྱེའོ། ། མི་དང་མི་མ་ཡིན་པ་དང་། གཅན་གཟན་གྱིས་འཇིགས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་
གྲོལ་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། ། ནད་དང་གདོན་ཐམས་ཅད་ལས་ཐར་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། ། ཨོཾ་མ་ཎི་པདྨ་ཧཱུྃ། ཞེས་བརྗོད་པས་འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་ཀྱི་ཞལ་མཐོང་བར་འགྱུར་ཞིང་ངོ་། ། ཚེ་འཕོས་ནས་ཀྱང་བདེ་བ་ཅན་དུ་
སྐྱེ་སྟེ། འདི་ལ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མམ། སོམ་ཉིའམ། ཡིད་གཉིས་མ་ཟ་ཅིག ། འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིག་དབང་ཕྱུག་གི་གཟུངས་རྫོགས་སོ།། །། ༄༅། ། སངས་རྒྱས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། །
ཆོས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། ། དགེ་འདུན་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། ། འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་དབང་པོ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། ། དེ་རྣམས་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ནས་རིག་པ་འདི་བརྗོད་

will become peaceful. He will become a protector for those without protection. I too grant this and rejoice! The Blessed One said: Then the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Samantabhadra spoke these bases of the secret mantra of the Great Queen of Knowledge-Mantras called "The Mother of Avalokiteshvara": I prostrate to the Triple Gem! I prostrate to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Amitabha! I prostrate to the Noble Lord Avalokiteshvara, the Bodhisattva Mahasattva endowed with great compassion! Having prostrated to them, I shall speak these bases of the secret mantra of the Great Queen of Knowledge-Mantras called "The Mother of Avalokiteshvara." May this knowledge be accomplished for me! <term>Tadyatha / Ili Mili / Tsili Mili / Kushule / Kushulesiri / Sisiri / Visiri / Virayu / Gori / Garbhari / Dramiri / Matadhdhia / Pukkasi / Kañtsaya / Mala Tsandali / Tsindu Dhudhuma Lini / Tsili Mili / Brihna Sosya Dedvani / Kushu Tsandramukhe / Labhumanya Ti / Arya Dakrina Bhuje / Sarva Vidvanama / Prasadha Ni / Sarva Vidvanama</term>. This is the ritual for this dharani which is accomplished by reading: Immediately upon hearing it, all karmic obscurations will be purified. It protects from all fears. If recited at the three times of day, then within seven days
<leaf-break/>
four-armed. The first two have palms joined. The lower right holds a white pearl rosary. The lower left holds a white lotus. The body color is white, seated in the full vajra posture, adorned with various jewel ornaments and a beautiful jewel crown. Supported by the six goddesses and the jewel <term>Avanorgu</term>, surrounded by many Bodhisattvas and female Bodhisattvas, it says this:
Thus he spoke. If a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family recites this mantra even once, or remembers it, or holds it in mind, or wears it on the body after writing it down, or acts with faith and devotion, all the five heinous crimes and nearly equivalent sinful karmas will be purified. They will not be reborn in the three lower realms, the eight unfree states, or with suffering. They will be liberated from all fears of humans, non-humans, and wild beasts. They will be freed from all diseases and demons. By reciting <term>Om Mani Padme Hum</term>, one will see the face of Noble Avalokiteshvara. After passing away, one will be born in Sukhavati. Do not have doubt, hesitation, or a dual mind about this. The Dharani of Noble Avalokiteshvara is complete.
I prostrate to the Buddha! I prostrate to the Dharma! I prostrate to the Sangha! I prostrate to the Noble Lord of Sight <note>Avalokiteshvara</note>, the Bodhisattva Mahasattva! Having prostrated to them, I speak this knowledge.

༼༽༔ ༔འདུ་ཤེས་ཕུང་པོ་རང་དག་ནས༔ པདྨ་རིགས་ཀྱི྾ པདྨ་ཨ྾ ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིགས་ཀྱི྾ རྒྱ་གྲཾ་འབར་བའི་དབང་྾ འདུ་བྱེད་ཕུང་པོ་རང་྾ ལས་ཀྱི་རིགས་ཀྱི྾ ༔
ཀརྨ་ཨ྾ ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིས་ཀྱི྾ འཁོར་ལོ་འབར་བའི྾ ༔ གཟུགས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་རང་྾ ༔ བདེ་གཤེགས་རིགས་ཀྱི྾ ༔ བུདྡྷ་ཨ྾ ༔ རྒྱལ་དབང་དྲག་དབང་བསྐུར་ནི྾ ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིགསཀྱི྾༔
ཞི་བ་ཟླུམ་པོའི་དབང་྾ ། ནད་གདོན་སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ཞི་ནས་ཀྱང་ ཞི་བའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་འགྲུབ་པར་ཤོག་ ༔ ཞི་བ་ཤནྟིཾ་ཀུ་རུ་ཡེ་སྭཱཧཱ ༔ ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིགས་གྱི་བུ་ཁྱོད་ལ ༔ རྒྱས་པ་གྲུ་བཞིའི་དབང་྾ ། ཚེ་དང་
བསོད་ནཾས་རྒྱས་ནས་ཀྱང་ ། རྒྱས་པའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་འགྲུབ་པརཤོག ༔ པུཥྚིཾ་ཀུ་རུ་ཡེ་སྭཱཧཱ ། ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིགས་ཀྱཻ྾ ། ཟླ་གམ་དབང་གི་དབང་བསྐུར་བས ། ཁཾས་གསུཾ་སྲིད་གསུཾ་དབང་བསྡུད་ནས །
དབང་གི་འཕྲིན་ལས་འགྲུབ་པར ཤོག ། པ་ཤཾ་ཀུ་རུ་ཡེ་སྭཱཧཱ ། ། ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིག་ཀྱི྾ ། དྲག་པོ་གྲུ་གསུམ་དབང་བསྐུར་བས ། དགྲ་བགེགས་མ་རུང་ཚར་གཅོད་ནས ། དྲག་པོའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་འགྲུབ་པར་ཤོག།
མཱ་ར་ཡ་ཧཱུཾ་ཕཊ ། དེ་ནས་གཏོར་མའི་དབང་བསྐུར་བ་ནི ། འདི་སྐད་དོ ། ཧཱུཾ࿒ སྐལ་ལྡན་རིས་ཀྱི་བུ་ཁྱོད་ལ ། གཏོར་མ་ཞི་རྒྱས་དབང་དྲག་གིས ། དབང་མཆོག་དམ་པ་བསྐུར་བ་ཡིས ། འཕྲིན་ལས་རྣཾ་བཞི་འགྲུབ་ནས་ཀྱང་ །
<leaf-break/>
༼༈༽༔ ༔སྦྱིན་པར་བྱ༔ ༢ ཡིས་དཀར་ཞིང་འཁྲུལ་སྣང་འགག༔ ༣ རྨི་ལཾ་ཤར་རྩེས་རས་སལ་པོར་སྟོན༔ ཅེས་བརྗོད་ལ་བུ་ལ་སྦྱིན་ནོ༔ དེ་ནས་སློབ་བུ་རྩུབས་ཉལ་ཁར་མགོ་ཁྱབ་ཁ་ནུབ༔ རྐང་པ་ལྷོར་བསྟན་པ༔ སེངྒེའི་ཉལ་སྟབས་བྱམས་ལ་ཉལ་ལོ༔ དེ་དུས་ཀུ་
ཤོ་ཉག་གཅིག་པདྨ་གཡས་པའི་གདན་དུ་བཏིང༔ ཉག་གཅིག་སྣ་མཆོག་གཡོན་པའི་གང་ཐུབ་ལ༔ སྨོན་ལཾ་བབ་པའི༔ བླ་མ་ཡི་དམ་མཁའགྲོ་དང་༔ ཆོས་སྐྱོང་དམ་ཅན་གཏེར་བདག་རྣཾས༔ དགེ་དང་མི་དགེའི་ལེགས་ཉེས་རྣཾས༔ རྨི་ལཾ་འཁྲུལ་
སྣང་ནང་ནས་མངོན་སུམ་བསྟེན་དུ་གསོལ༔ ཅེས་བརྗོད་ཅིང་མི་སྐྱེ་བར་ཉལ་ལོ༔ ནང་པར་རྨི་ལམ་གང་བྱུང་རྣཾས༔ རྡོེ་སློབ་དཔོན་གྱི་དྲུང་དུ་བཤད༔ བཟང་རྟགས་རྣཾས་ནི་འདི་ལྟར་ཏེ༔ དབང་ཆེན་འབྱར་དང་དྱུ་ཆེན་འབུད༔ ཉི་ཟླ་ཤར་དང་རྨ་གོས་བཟང་༔ ཆུས་སྐྱ་ལ་
བྱེད་གྱེན་ལ་འཐོ༔ དེ་དག་རྣཾས་ཞི་བ་ཐར་པོའི་རྟགས༔ ངན་རྟགས་རྣཾས་ཞི་འདི་ལྟར་རོ༔ ཁབ་སྟོང་གྲོག་སྟོང་འགྲིམ་པ་དང༔ མཚོན་ཆ་ཆག་དང་གོས་ཧྲུལ་གོན༔ ཉི་ཟླ་ནུབ་དང་ས་སྲོལ་དང༔ མིུ་ཏོག་དམར་པོ་འཐུ་བ་དང༔ བྱོལ་སོང་ཕྱིར་སོག་ཞོན་པ་དང༔ དེ་རྣཾས་དྲི་མ་ནང་ནས་པའི་རྟགས༔ བཟང་པོ་
རྣཾས་ལ་བསྔོ་བྱ༔ ཞལ་རྣཾས་ལ་གཏོར་ཆོགས་བཟློག་པ་བྱ༔ དེ་ནས་སྦྱིན་བསྲེག་བྱ་བ་ནི༔ སྒྲུབ་ཁང་དེའི་སྒོ་དྲུང་དུ༔ མ་ཏྲཾ་གན་རྒྱལ་སྐྱེས་བའི་སྟེང༔ དྲག་པོའི་ཤིང་ནི་གྲུ་གསུམ་བརྩིགས༔ དེ་ལ་སྲེག་རྫས་འདི་ལྟར་རོ༔ འབྲུ་སྣ་ལྔ་དང་རིན་ཆེན་ལྔ༔ སྐྲ་དང་སེ་ན་མོ་མཆིལ་སྣབས་དང༔ ཟས་
སྣ་ཆ་བདུན་ཤ་སྣ་དང༔ སྨན་སྣ་སྤྲོས་རྣམས་བསྲེག་པར་བྱ༔ ཐབ་ནང་དབང་ཆེན་བསྐྱེད་ལ་འབུལ༔ བདག་ཅག་རྣཾས་ཀྱི་ནད་གདོན་སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་རྔམས་ཅད་ང་རྒྱཾ་ཀུ་རུ་ཡེ་སྭཱཧཱ༔ ཚེ་དང་བསོད་ནཾས་དཔལ་དང་འབྱོར་པ་ཐཾད་རྒྱས་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག༔ པུ་ཥྚིཾ་ཀུ་རུ་
<leaf-break/>
༁ཾ༔ ༔ ཕྱིར་བསྔོ༔ བསྐྱིལ་བརྔོག་བཞེ༔ ཞེ་སྡང་འཇོཾས་མཛད་བཛྲ་རྟ་མཆོག་དཔལ༔ ཞི་བའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་མཐར་ཕྱིན་བཀྲིས་ཤོག༔ ང་རྒྱལ་འཇོམས་མཛད་རཏྣ་རྟ་མཆོག་དཔལ༔ རྒྱས་པའི་ཕྲིནས་
མཐར་ཕྱིན྾༔ འདོད་ཆགས་འཇོཾས་མཛད་པདྨ་རྟ་མཆོག་དཔལ༔ དབང་གི་འཕྲིན་ལས་མཐར་ཕྱིན྾༔ ཕྲ་དོག་འཇོཾས་མཛད་ཀརྨ་རྟ་མཆོག་དཔལ༔ དྲག་པོའི་འཕྲིན་ལས་མཐར་ཕྱིན། ༔ གཏི་མུག་འཇོཾས་མཛད་
བུ་དྡྷ་རྟ་མཆོག་དཔལ༔ ལྷུན་གྲུབ་འཕྲིན་ལས་མཐར་ཕྱིན༔ མཆོག་དང་ཐུན་མོང་དངོས་གྲུབ་སྟེར་མཛད་པའི༔ ཡི་དཾ་ལྷ་ཚོགས་རྣཾས་ཀྱི་༴ ལུང་བསྟན་སྟོང་གྲོགས་བྱེད་མཛད་པ༔ མ་དང་མཁའགྲོའི་༴ བར་
ཆད་རྐྱེན་རྣཾས་ཀུན་སེལ་བ༔ ཆོས་སྐྱོང་གཏེར་བདག་྾ ། རྡོེ་སློབ་དཔོན་མཆེད་ལྕམ་རྣཾས་༴ མི་འབྲལ་འགྲོགས་པའི་྾ ། ཅེས་བགྱིས་བརྗོད་དོ། དེ་ནས་དབང་གི་དབང་གི་དགའ་སྟོན་བྱ་བ་ནི༔ བྲོ་བརྡུང་གླུ་བླངས་ཉཾས་བསྐྱང་
བར་བྱའོ༔ སྟ་གོན་གྱི་དབང་མཆོག་རྡོེ་གོ་ཁྲབ་འདི༔ པདྨང་ཡིས་ཕྱི་རབས་དོན་དུ་བཀོད༔ རིན་ཆེན་ས་ལག་ཏེར་དུ་སྦས༔ འདི་འཆང་སྐྱེས་བུ་ལས་ཅན་ནི༔ པདྨའི་མིང་ཅན་རྟ་སྦྲུལ་ལོ༔ ཚིག་རྩུབ་ལྟ་སྐད་ཆོ་ལེ་སྨྲ༔ སྐལྡན་
དེ་དང་འཕྲད་པར་ཤོག༔ ས་མ་ཡ༔ རྒྱ་རྒྱ་རྒྱ༔ གཏེར་རྒྱ༔ གཏད་རྒྱ༔ སྦས་རྒྱ༔ བཀའ་རྒྱ༔ དམ་རྒྱ༔ གསང་རྒྱ༔ བདག་པདྨ་གླིང་པས་ ལྷོ་བྲག་སྨན་མདོ་ནས་གདན་དྲངས་པའོ། །།

...The aggregate of perception itself is purified; the [empowerment] of the Lotus family... *Padma A...* *Hum!* Upon the fortunate one of the family... the empowerment of the blazing crossed-vajra... the aggregate of formations itself... of the Activity family... 
*Karma A...* *Hum!* Upon the fortunate one of the family... the empowerment of the blazing wheel... the aggregate of form itself... of the Tathagata family... 
*Buddha A...* The conferral of the empowerment of the Victorious Power and Wrathful Power: *Hum!* Upon the fortunate one of the family... 
the empowerment of the peaceful circle... having pacified sickness, spirits, sins, and obscurations, may the peaceful activity be accomplished! *Shantim kuru ye svaha!* *Hum!* Upon you, the fortunate child of the family, 
the empowerment of the increasing square... having increased life and merit, may the increasing activity be accomplished! *Pushtim kuru ye svaha!* *Hum!* Upon the fortunate one of the family... 
by conferring the power of the semi-circular Magnetizing empowerment, having brought the three realms and three existences under control, may the magnetizing activity be accomplished! *Pasham kuru ye svaha!* *Hum!* Upon the fortunate one of the family... 
by conferring the wrathful triangular empowerment, having cut down the unsuitable enemies and obstructors, may the wrathful activity be accomplished! 
*Maraya hum phat!* Then the conferral of the <term>torma</term> <gloss>ritual cake</gloss> empowerment is as follows: *Hum!* Upon you, the fortunate child of the family, 
by the torma of peace, increase, power, and wrath, and by conferring the supreme and sacred empowerment, having accomplished the four activities...

<leaf-break/>

...should be given. Through the two [stalks], white [kusha] and the cessation of illusory appearances. Three: the appearance of the peak of dreams shows things clearly. Having said this, give them to the child. Then, when the student goes to sleep, the head is covered and pointed west, 
the feet pointed south; sleep in the lion's posture with love. At that time, a single stalk of <term>kusha</term> grass is spread as a mat under the right [side]. Another single stalk is placed [under the pillow] as much as possible for the best... 
whichever prayer falls: "Gurus, <term>Yidams</term>, and <term>Dakinis</term>, and the Dharma Protectors, Oath-bound ones, and Treasure Lords; the virtues and non-virtues, the good and the bad; 
please show them clearly within the illusory appearances of dreams." Having said this, sleep without speaking. In the morning, explain whatever dreams occurred 
in the presence of the <term>Vajra</term> Master. The good signs are as follows: the Great Powerful One clinging or a great banner flying; 
the sun and moon rising and wearing good clothes; crossing a bridge over water and going upwards—these are all signs of peace and liberation. The bad signs are as follows: wandering through empty needles or empty anthills; 
broken weapons or wearing ragged clothes; the sun and moon setting or the twilight; picking red flowers; riding backward on an animal—these are signs of stains from within. 
One should dedicate the good ones. For the bad ones, perform the <term>torma</term> ritual for averting. Then, as for the fire offering: at the gate of that practice house, 
on top of a supine <term>Matram</term> spirit, stack wrathful wood in a triangle. The substances for burning are as follows: the five types of grain and five precious things; 
hair, fingernails, saliva, and snot; the seven parts of various foods and various meats; various medicines—these should be burnt. 
Visualize the Great Powerful One within the hearth and offer. All the sickness, spirits, sins, and obscurations of us all—*Nga-gyam kuru ye svaha!* May life, merit, glory, and wealth all increase! *Pushtim kuru...*

<leaf-break/>

...dedicate for others. Restrict, turn back, and accept. The one who destroys hatred: the Glorious Vajra Hayagriva. May there be the auspiciousness of completing the peaceful activities! 
The one who destroys pride: the Glorious Ratna Hayagriva. May there be the completion of the increasing activities... The one who destroys desire: the Glorious Padma Hayagriva. May there be the completion of the magnetizing activities... 
The one who destroys jealousy: the Glorious Karma Hayagriva. May there be the completion of the wrathful activities! The one who destroys ignorance: 
the Glorious Buddha Hayagriva. May there be the completion of spontaneously accomplished activities! Those who grant supreme and common accomplishments: 
to the hosts of <term>Yidam</term> deities... Those who provide prophecies and help: of the Mothers and <term>Dakinis</term>... Those who clear away all obstacles and conditions: 
Dharma Protectors and Treasure Lords... To the <term>Vajra</term> Master and the brothers and sisters... of being inseparable companions... thus recites the dedication. 
Then, for the feast of the empowerment: perform dances, sing songs, and sustain the experience. This "Vajra Armor" of the supreme preparatory empowerment was composed by me, Padma, for the sake of future generations. 
It was hidden as a treasure in the precious earth. The karmically endowed person who will hold this is one named Padma, born in the year of the Horse or Snake. 
Harsh in speech, talking like a lunatic. May it meet with that fortunate one. <term>Samaya</term>. Seal, seal, seal. Treasure seal. Entrustment seal. Hidden seal. Command seal. Commitment seal. Secret seal. 
I, Pema Lingpa, invited this from Mando in Lhodrak.

༄༅། །མཛོད།། །།དེ་ནས་རྗེས་གནང་བྱ་བ་ནི་དབུ་མ་པ་སྟ་གོན་བྱས་པའི་རྗེས་ སློབ་མ་ཁྲུས་བྱས་གྲལ་ལ་འཁོད་། བགེགས་བསྐྲད་མཎྜལ་ཕུལ་། གསོལ་བཏབ་ན་ནི། དགོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ལན་གསུམ་བརྗོད་། སློབ་མ་སེང་གད་དོར་རིགས་ལྔ་གོང་ལྟར་བསྒོམ་དུ་བཅུག་། ཨོཾ་ཨཱཿཧཱུཾ་
ལས་འོད་འཕྲོས་། མཁའ་འགྲོ་མའི་སྐ་ལས་ཡེ་ཤེས་བདུད་རྩིའི་ཆར་བབ་། ཁྱེད་རང་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ལུས་ལ་ཐིམ་། རོལ་མོ་དང་། ཨོཾ་ཨཱཿ ཧྲཱི་ཧྲཱིཿཕེཾ་ཕེཾ་། མེ་ཏོག་དོར་རྡོ་རྗེ་མགོ་ཐོག་བཞག །སུ་པྲ་ཏིཥྛ་བརྗོད་། ཀུན་མཁྱེན་
ཡེ་ཤེས་ལན་གསུམ་། གཏོར་མ་མགོ་ཐོག་བཞག །བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མའི་དཔྲལ་བ་ནས་འོད་ཟེར་དཀར་པོ་རྒྱུན་དུ་བྱུང་། ཁྱེད་རང་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་དཔྲལ་བར་ཐིམ་། ལུས་ཀྱི་སྒྲིབ་པ་དག །སྐུའི་དབང་ཐོབ་། ནང་མཆོད་
མེ་ཏོག་གཏོར་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མའི་ཐུགས་ཁར་ས་བོན་སྔགས་ཀྱི་འཕྲེང་བས་བསྐོར་བ་ཞལ་ལས་བྱུང་། ཁྱེད་རང་རྣམས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མར་གསལ་བའི་ཞལ་ནས་ཞུགས་། ཐུགས་ཁར་ས་བོན་སྔགས་འཕྲེང་
ལ་ཐིམ་། སྔགས་ཀྱི་དངོས་གྲུབ་ཐོབ་པར་གྱུར་། སྔགས་བགྲང་། འཕྲེང་བ་མགྲིན་པར་བཞག །ནང་མཆོད་འབུལ་ངགི་སྒྲིབ་པ་དག །གསུང་གི་དབང་ཐོབ་། མེ་ཏོག་གོང་དང་འདྲ་། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་མའི་ཐུགསཁར་
ནས་ཕྱག་མཚན་གྱི་རྣམ་པ་བྱུང་། ཁྱེད་རང་རྣམས་གྱིས་སྙིང་ཁར་ཐིམ་། ཡིད་ཀྱི་སྒྲིབ་པ་དག །ཐུགས་ཀྱི་དབང་ཐོབ་། མེ་ཏོག་དང་སུ་པྲ་ཏིཥྛ་བརྗོད་། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རིགས་ལྔ་སྤྱི་བོར་བྱོན་། ནད་གདོན་བགེགས་
<leaf-break/>
ནས་བླུག་པར་བསམ་ལ་སྔགས་བགྲང་། སྟོང་རྩ་རེ་བགྲང་ན་ཚེ་ཉི་ཟླ་དང་མཉམ་མོ། །ནོར་སྒྲུབ་ནི། རང་མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་དམར་མོ་ཕྱག་གཡས་ན་ཡིད་བཞིན་ནོར་བུའི་རྒྱལ་མཚན་ནམ་མཁར་འཕྱར་བ།
གཡོན་པདྨའི་ཐོད་པ་རིན་པོ་ཆེས་གང་བ་ཐུགས་ཁར་འཛིན་པ། ཞབས་གཉིས་གར་ཐབས་སུ་བཞུགས་པ། རིན་པོ་ཆེ་རུས་པའི་རྒྱན་དྲུག་གསོལ་བ་སྒོམ་ལ་སྔགས་བཟླས་སོ། །འབུམ་ཚོགས་གཅིག་གི་འགྲུབ་
བོ། །དབང་འདུད་ནི། རང་སེང་གདོང་ནག་མོ་ཕྱག་གཡས་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་འཛིན་པ། ལྷ་འདྲེ་མི་གསུམ་གྱི་སྙིང་ནས་འཛིན་པ། གཡོན་གཏེར་གྱི་བུམ་པ་བཀུར་སྟེན་ལ། རྒྱན་དྲུག་དང་ཞབས་གཉིས་གར་ཐབས་
སུ་བཞུགས་པ། ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་མེ་འབར་བར་སྒོམ་ལ་སྔགས་བཟླས། འགྲོ་བ་ཐམས་ཅད་དབང་དུ་སྡུས་ཅི་སྭཱ་ཧཱ། འབུམ་ཚོགས་གསུམ་བཟླས་སོ། །སྲིའུ་བསོ་བ་ནི། མི་གྲོ་ཤི་ཕོའི་རུས་པ། གུ་གུལ།
རྟ་བོན་གསུམ་ལ་སེང་གདོང་མའི་སྐུ་གསུང་ཐུགས་བསྐྱེད། སྔགས་སྟོང་རྩ་བདུན་བཏབ་ལ་ཞིབ་པར་རྟགས། བ་སྤུའི་ནང་དུ་བཅུག་ལ་ཚག་བྱས། ཕོ་མོ་གང་རུང་འདྲ། བུ་ཆུང་སྐྱེས་མ་ཐག་ལྟེ་ཐག་མ་ཆད་པ་
ལ་སྤྱི་བོར། རྣ་བ་གཉིས། སྲིན་འཛུག་གཉིས། སྙིང་ཁ། ཆུ་ཁ་འཕོང་། སྐྱེས་པ། རྐང་པའི་མཐེབ་སྲིན་བཞི་ལ། རྫས་ཀྱི་ཐིག་ལེ་བྱ། ཧཱུྃ་ནག་པོ་རེས་བསྲུང་བ་སྒོམ། ཧཱུྃ་རྣམས་མཁའ་འགྲོ་སྒོམ།
<leaf-break/>
ཅད་དགུག་གཞུག་བྱ ། དེའི་ནང་ན་དངོས་སུ་ཡོང་བ་བསམ ། དེའི་སྟེང་གི་ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་ཐིམ་པར་བསམ ། སྔགས་སུམ་བརྒྱ་འདེབས་སྤྲིན་འདུ་བ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མེད ། སེར་བ་བསྲུང་ན །
རང་སེང་གདོང་མར་སྒོམ ། སྔགས་སྟོང་རྩ་གཉིས་གནམ་ལ་འདེབས ། ཐོ་རང་བྱས་པས་སེར་བ་ཐུབ ། ལུག་ནད་སྤྱོད་ན ། དཀར་སྒོང་སྲིན་མེད་བྱེ་མ་བྲེད་ལ་དུག་ལུས་བྲན་ལ་སྔགས་སྟོང་རྩ་བཏབ །
སྒོ་ཁང་ལུག་གི་མདུན་ནས་བྲབ ། ལུག་ནད་ཐམས་ཅད་བྱ་སྒོམས་ཚིག་པར་བསམ ། ཐུབ་ངེས་སོ ། ། སྣ་ནད་བསྲུང་བ་ནི ། བས་དཀར་ནག་དམར་གསུམ་ལ་སྐུད་པ་གསུམ་སྒྲིལ་བྱས་ལ་མདུད་པ་
གསུམ་བོར་སྔགས་སྟོང་བཏབ་ལ་བཏགས་ན་སྣ་ནད་ཐུབ་པ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མེད ། ལྷོག་པ་བསྲུང་ན ། སྔགས་སྟོང་རྩ་རེ་བཟླས་ཏེ་ཆུ་ལ་བཏབ་ནས་བླུད་ན་ཐུབ་ངེས་སོ ། ། རིམས་ནད་བསྲུང་ན ། ཐག་
བོང་ནག་པོ་གཉིས་བསྲེག་ལ་སྔགས་བརྒྱ་བཏབ ། དེའི་དུད་པས་བདུག་ན་ཐུབ་པ་ཐེ་ཚོམ་མེད ། འབྲུམ་ནད་བསྲུང་ན ། སྲན་མ་བདུན་ལ་སྔགས་བརྒྱ་རྩ་བདུན་བཏབ་ནས་བཏགས་ན་
ཐུབ་ངེས་སོ ། ། འཁྲུམ་གཅོད་ན ། ཁྱི་བརྒྱ་འུའི་བས་བུ་མོ་གཙང་མས་སྨྱོས ། བུ་མོ་གཙང་མས་སྐལ་བའི་སྐུད་པ་ལ་སུམ་སྒྲིལ་ལ་སྔགས་སྟོང་རྩ་གཉིས་བཏབ་ནས །

Perform! Then, for the empowerment, after the preparatory ritual by the central master, the students perform ritual bathing and take their seats. Dispel obstacles and offer the mandala. If making a request, recite the Refuge in the Three Jewels three times. Have the students visualize the five families of the Lion-Faced One as before. Light radiates from the OM AH HUM. A rain of wisdom nectar falls from the bodies of the Dakinis. It dissolves into your bodies. Play music and recite OM AH HRI HRI PHEM PHEM. Toss flowers and place a vajra on the head. Recite SUPRATISHTHA. Recite the Wisdom of the Omniscient One three times. Place the ritual cake on the head. A stream of white light emerges from the forehead of the Blessed Lady. It dissolves into your foreheads. The obscurations of the body are purified. Obtain the empowerment of the Body. Sprinkle inner offering and flowers; from the heart of the Blessed Lady, the seed syllable surrounded by the mantra garland emerges from her mouth. It enters through the mouths of those visualized as the Blessed Lady. It dissolves into the seed syllable and mantra garland at the heart. May the accomplishment of the mantra be obtained. Recite the mantra. Place the mala beads at the throat. Offer the inner offering; the obscurations of speech are purified. Obtain the empowerment of Speech. The flowers are as before. From the heart of the Blessed Lady, the forms of the hand implements emerge. They dissolve into your hearts. The obscurations of the mind are purified. Obtain the empowerment of the Mind. Recite the flowers and SUPRATISHTHA. The Blessed Ones of the five families arrive at the crown. Diseases, demons, and obstacles

<leaf-break/>

Visualize the nectar pouring into you and recite the mantra. If you recite it one thousand times, your life will be equal to the sun and moon. For the wealth practice: Visualize yourself as the Red Dakini, holding a victory banner of the wish-fulfilling jewel toward the sky in your right hand. In the left, you hold a lotus skull cup filled with jewels at your heart. You dwell in a dancing posture with two legs. Wear the six ornaments of bone and jewels; recite the mantra. Accomplishment comes with one hundred thousand repetitions. For magnetizing: Visualize yourself as the Black Lion-Faced One holding an iron hook in the right hand. You seize the hearts of gods, demons, and humans. In the left, you hold a treasure vase. Wearing the six ornaments and dwelling in a dancing posture with two legs, visualize the fire of wisdom blazing and recite the mantra. SUBJUGATE ALL BEINGS CI SVAHA. Recite three hundred thousand times. For protecting a child: Use the bone of a man who died of a chronic illness, incense <term>gugul</term>, and horse dung. Generate the body, speech, and mind of the Lion-Faced One. Bless them with one thousand and seven repetitions and mark them clearly. Place them inside a hair and seal it. It is the same for male or female. Immediately after a child is born, before the umbilical cord is cut, apply dots of the substance to the crown, the two ears, the two ring fingers, the heart, the urethra, the anus, the genitals, and the four toes. Visualize being protected by a black HUM. Visualize the HUMs as Dakinis.

<leaf-break/>

Perform the summoning and entering. Visualize the actual presence coming within. Visualize them dissolving into the space above. Recite the mantra three hundred times; there is no doubt the clouds will gather. If protecting against hail: Visualize yourself as the Lion-Faced One. Recite the mantra one thousand and two times toward the sky. By doing this at dawn, hail can be stopped. If treating sheep disease: Use a white egg without a germ, mix with sand, sprinkle it on the body of the sick animal, and recite the mantra one thousand times. Sprinkle it from the front of the sheep pen. Visualize all sheep diseases being burned like a bird's wing in fire. It is certain to work. For protecting against "nose-disease" <note>likely a livestock respiratory illness</note>: Twist together three threads of white, black, and red cow hair, tie three knots, recite the mantra one thousand times, and tie it; there is no doubt the nose-disease will be stopped. If protecting against <term>lhokpa</term> <gloss>ulcerous sores or plague</gloss>: Recite the mantra one thousand times over water and give it to drink; it is certain to work. For protecting against contagious fever: Burn the hair of a black donkey and recite the mantra one hundred times. If you fumigate with the smoke, there is no doubt it will be stopped. For protecting against smallpox: Recite the mantra one hundred and seven times over seven peas and wear them; it is certain to work. To stop diarrhea: Have a pure young girl spin the hair of a hundred dogs. The pure girl should triple-twist the thread of the portion and recite the mantra one thousand and two times.

༁ྃ༔ ལ་བཀྲིས་པ༔ ཕྱག་ན་ཀླུའི་ཐོད་པ་སྔོ་སིང་ངི་བ༔ གསེར་གི་བྱུར་གྱིས་བཀང(ས)་པའི་སྟེངས་སུ༔ གསེར་གི་སྤ་
ཁྲ་བཞགས་པ་བསྣམས་པ༔ འོད་ཟེར་སྣ་ཚོགསུ་འཕྲོ་བ་གཅིག་རྒྱལ་པོའི་དྲུང་དུ་འོངས་ནས༔ གསེར་འཕུལ་སྟེ་འདི་
སྐད་གསུངས་སོ༔ ཀྱཻ་རྒྱལ་པོ་ཆེན་པོ་ལགས་བདག་ནི་མལ་གྲོ་ཀླུའི་སྡེ་དཔོན་ཡིན༔ ནག་པོ་ཀློང་རྡོལ་ཞེས་
པའི་གནས་ནས་འོངས༔ བདག་དང་འགྲོག་པོ་འདི་རིང་སྣ་མཐོ་ཅད་༔ བསམ་ཡས་ལྷའི་གསེར་རྣཾས་བདགིས་འབྱིན༔
ཅེས་གསུང་ནས༔ རྒྱལ་པོ་ཉིད་དང་མལ་གྲོའི་ཀླུ་གཉིས་ཀྱིས་སློབ་དཔོན་པདྨ་འབྱུང་གནས་སྤངས་པོར་གཞག་

Auspicious. In his hand, he held a <term>Naga</term> <gloss>serpent-spirit</gloss> skull of a brilliant deep blue, filled with golden coral, upon which was placed a golden cane-spear. This being, emitting various rays of light, came before the King, offered the gold, and spoke thus: "O Great King, I am the chief of the <term>Mal-gro</term> Naga clan. I come from the place called the Black Spilling Abyss. From today, we are companions. I will provide the gold for the gods of Samye." Having said this, the King and the Naga of Mal-gro took the Master Padmasambhava as their witness and vowed to be companions like brothers. They cut [the top of] their noses <note>a traditional form of oath-taking</note>, and the King [began] the Naga-palace...
<leaf-break/>
"O Master, show me your ultimate form; it is needed for the construction of the Naga-house. This small boy's form lacks majesty and cannot be captured in a clay statue. Therefore, tomorrow when you come, do not manifest as a small boy, but show yourself as you truly are." The Naga replied: "I will come tomorrow. Since there is a danger of my companion being struck by poison, smear some <term>la-tsi</term> <gloss>soul-substance/musk</gloss> on an iron mask and wear it on your face. Stay in the lower Yaksha-ling, and when the sun rises over the mountain peak, look toward the central pinnacle." Then the King went from the central pinnacle and stayed the night in the lower Yaksha-ling. In his dreams, he saw many magical displays of the lords of the soil. The King's heart was not at ease.
<leaf-break/>
Those living beings with mental bodies, in the places where they reside as foundations within the body, all the channels twitched. All the flesh burned <term>tsa tsak tsak</term>, pained <term>na tsak tsak</term>, itched <term>ya tsak tsak</term>, throbbed <term>na kar kar</term>, stung <term>tsa be ber ber</term>, seared <term>tsa breng breng</term>, blazed <term>brang lhang lhang</term>, thrummed <term>tsa bhir bhir</term>, itched <term>ya bhir bhir</term>, went numb <term>sprid chil chil</term>, boiled <term>za khol khol</term>, whistled <term>tse shum shum</term>, and scattered <term>sro byer byer</term>. The entire body was completely uncomfortable. He deeply regretted asking the Naga to show his form. Now, the eighteen different kinds of leprosy had gathered in one month and emerged from the human skin. Although he had previously been a leader of men, now he did not even fit among the ranks of the wretched. Thinking this, he was oppressed by great suffering, could not remain on his seat, and his "heart-wind" <gloss>anxiety/agitation</gloss> arose. The Naga of Mal-gro, seeing that the King had been struck by poison, felt ashamed and embarrassed, and his offering of gold was interrupted.

ཆོས་འདུལ་བ་འདི་ལ་ནི། འཕགས་པའི་ལམ་ཡན་ལགབརྒྱད་པ་ཡོད་པས་ན། དགེ་སྦྱོང་དང་པོ་ཡང་འདི་ལ་ཡོད་དོ། །གཉིས་པ་ཡང་འདི་ལ་ཡོད་དོ། ། གསུམ་པ་ཡང་འདི་ལ་ཡོད་དོ།། བཞི་
པ་ཡང་འདི་ལ་ཡོད་དོ། འདི་ལས་ཕྱི་རོལ་པ་ལ་ནི་དགེ་སྦྱོང་དང་བྲམ་ཟེ་མེད་ལ། ཕས་ཀྱི་རྒོལ་བ་དག་ནི་དགེ་སྦྱོང་རྣམས་དང་བྲམ་ཟེ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་སྟེ། ང་ནི་འདིར་འཁོར་གྱི་ནང་དུ་དེ་སྐད་
ཅེས་ཡང་དག་པར་སེང་གེའི་སྒྲ་སྒྲོགས་སོ། །ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་བཤད་པ་ན་ཀུན་ཏུ་རྒྱུ་རབ་བཟང་ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་མིག་རྡུལ་མེད་ཅིང་དྲི་མ་དང་བྲལ་བ་སྐྱེས་ཏེ། ཀུན་ཏུ་རྒྱུ་རབ་
བཟང་གིས་ཆོས་མཐོང་། ཆོས་རྙེད། ཆོས་རྟོགས། ཆོས་ཀྱི་གཏིང་སླེབས། སོམ་ཉི་ལས་རྒལ་ཐེ་ཙོམ་ལས་རྒལ་ནས། སྟོན་པའི་བསྟན་པ་ལ་གཞན་གྱི་དྲིང་མི་འཇོག་ཅིང་གཞན་གྱིས་བཀྲི་
pages.translation:
"Tathagatas, Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, only occasionally appear in the world; they are like the <term>udumbara</term> flower <note>A legendary flower that blooms once every three thousand years</note>. Since Gautama will pass into final nirvana in the sphere of nirvana without remainder tonight at midnight, and I have uncertainties and doubts regarding the teachings, and I have the hope that Gautama can remove those uncertainties of mine, Ananda, if it is no trouble for you, and if there is an opportunity to ask for a prophecy, I would enter and ask a few points." Then the Venerable Ananda said again to the wanderer Subhadra: "Subhadra, the Blessed One is weary; the Sugata's body is exhausted. Leave it, Subhadra, do not disturb the Blessed One." Then the Blessed One heard that conversation between the Venerable Ananda and the wanderer Subhadra with his divine ear, which is pure and transcends that of humans. Having heard it, he spoke to the Venerable Ananda: "Ananda, do not say that! Do not hinder the wanderer Subhadra; let him enter and ask whatever he wishes. This is my last conversation with other heretical wanderers."

<leaf-break/>

"I have meditated with a one-pointed mind. Even the mere mention of the side of the logical Dharma does not exist among other ascetics outside of this. Subhadra, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya <gloss>discipline</gloss> the Noble Eightfold Path is not found, in that, the first ascetic <note>the Stream-enterer</note> is not found. In that, the second <note>Once-returner</note>, the third <note>Non-returner</note>, and the fourth ascetic <note>Arhat</note> are also not found. Subhadra, in whatever Dharma and Vinaya the Noble Eightfold Path is found, in that, the first ascetic is found. The second, third, and fourth ascetics are found. Subhadra, since this Dharma and Vinaya possesses the Noble Eightfold Path, the first ascetic is found in it. The second is found in it. The third is found in it. The fourth is found in it. Outside of this, there are no ascetics or Brahmins; other schools are empty of ascetics and Brahmins. Here, within the assembly, I thus truly roar the lion's roar!" While this discourse on the Dharma was being explained, the stainless and pure Dharma-eye arose in the wanderer Subhadra regarding the teachings. The wanderer Subhadra saw the Dharma, attained the Dharma, realized the Dharma, and reached the depths of the Dharma. Having crossed beyond uncertainty and doubt, he no longer relied on others regarding the Teacher's teaching—

Blue, white, red, yellow, green, and so on—all the various kinds. All shall transform into their own light. Perform the activity of leading *Om* and primordial wisdom! *A yu jñana bin du bhrum*. *Tshe bhrum*. *Ni bhrum*. *Yu ti bhrum*. *A bhrum*. Then, for the mass of pellets, the nature of empowerment is in the rolling. In the single mandala of the deity, they are rolled into a single family. Within that, life and primordial wisdom are rolled together. *Hum*. Blessed One of Great Power, Lord of Magnetizing, Lord of Life and Lord of Magnetizing, Lord of Life and Primordial Wisdom! In the single mass of the heart mandala, the unchanging, indestructible vajra life. Because of being refined, the unchanging pure dharma. It is difficult even for all the Buddhas to see. By sealing with the four mudras, that seal cannot be destroyed by anyone. Life is placed in the *dharmadhatu* <note>the sphere of reality</note>. The mudra is clear but lacks inherent nature. First is the dharma mudra. Second is the mantra and mudra seal. Third is the body and primordial wisdom seal. Fourth is the seal of the four primordial wisdoms. Fifth is the seal of the five families' primordial wisdom. Sixth is the seal of the Buddhas in general. Seventh is the seal of the primordial wisdom of enlightenment. After sealing in that way, then that seal should be opened. Then, arise to attain the *siddhis*. That is the meeting with the ultimate meaning.

<leaf-break/>

Regarding the remaining: Binding the right hand in a fist and gesturing to strike with the left is the mudra of the great charnel ground. After firmly interlocking the ten fingers, the manner of blocking the path of the six realms is the mudra for purifying the lower realms. After firmly interlocking the two thumbs and extending the other eight upwards, this is the mudra of the spontaneously accomplished gathered families. For each mudra there is a syllable; from each syllable light radiates. This is known as the striking of mantra and mudra. Furthermore, the manner of moving, the postures, the shifting of the dance, and the performing of the dance are said to be the offering of the mudra. Thus it was said. From the *Tantra of the Play of the Supreme Horse*, this is the one hundred and ninth chapter, concerning the expansion of mantra and mudra. Then again, Vajrapani <note>Vajra-in-Hand</note> petitioned the King of Empowerment in this way: "How wonderful, Great King who embodies all Buddhas! What is meant by 'Horse'? To what does 'Supreme' refer? To what does 'Play' refer? What is meant by 'Tantra'? May the King who embodies all give the command! I wish to listen to the supreme embodiment of all." Thus he petitioned. The embodiment of Great Power gave the command: "Nirmanakaya <note>Emanation Body</note>..."

༄༅། །པར་གཟིར་བར་བྱོས། །ཟུང་ཞིག་རྒྱོབ་ཅིག་རྣམ་པར་ཆིངས། །རིངས་པར་ཁུག་ལ་སྣར་ཆུག་ཅིག །ང་ཡི་དབང་དུ་གྱུར་ནས་ཀྱང་། །བསྒོ་བའི་བཀའ་འདི་ཉན་པར་བྱོས། །ཞལ་
དུ་བསྟབ་པོ་མགུལ་དུ་བསྟིམས། །སྐུའི་གཟི་བརྗིད་རྒྱས་པར་མཛོད། །བཛྲ་ཡཀྵ་ཀྲོ་དྷ་ཁ་ཐཾ་ཁ་ཐཾ་ཁཱ། ཁཱ་ཧི་ཁཱ་ཧི་ཁ་ཧི། ཧཱ་ཧཱ་ཧཱ། ཧཱུྃ་ཧཱུྃ་ཧཱུྃ། ཕཊ་ཕཊ་ཕཊ། ཕུར་པ་ཉི་ཤུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད་ལ། །ཡབ་ཡུམ་
གསུམ་གྱི་བདེན་གཉིས་ཀྱིས། །ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོའི་སྐུ་རུ་གསུང་། །ཛ་ཏིས་འགུག་སེ་དང་གསང་པའི་མཆོག །སྲས་ཀྱི་མཆོག་གིས་ལས་རྣམས་འགྲུབ། །ཁྲོ་བོ་ཨོུཾ་བཅུ་པོ་ཡིས། །གནས་བཅུ་དུག་གསུཾ་
རྩད་ནས་གཅོད། །སྒོ་བ་བཞི་ཡིས་མཚོ་བཞི་བསྐེམས། །སྲིད་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕུར་པའི་ལྷ། །ཡེ་ཤེས་ཁྲོ་བོར་རབ་བསྒྲུབ་ནས། །ཉོན་མོངས་དུག་ལྔ་རྩད་ནས་གཅོད། །ཁྲག་འཐུང་རིགས་ལྔ་འདུས་པ་ལས། །
རྡོ་རྗེ་གཞོན་ནུའི་དངོས་གྲུབ་ཐོབ། །ལས་བཞི་གྲུབ་པའི་སྨོན་ལམ་གདབ། །གང་ཞིག་མཚོན་ཆ་མང་པོ་དང་། །མཚོན་ཆ་འཕྲེང་བ་ཡིག་འབྲུ་དང་། །སྒྲ་དང་མེ་དང་འོད་དང་འཇའ། །དྲག་བྱེད་ཐམས་ཅད་བྲན་
དུ་བཀོལ། །ཁྲག་མཚོ་ཤ་རུས་དཔུངས་པ་ཡི། །དྲག་བྱེད་ཀུན་ཏུ་མཐོང་པ་དང་། །འོད་དང་དུ་བ་མེ་རྣམས་བྱུང་། །ཚེ་དང་མི་འཕེལ་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་དང་། །རིགས་འཛིན་ས་དང་དབྱིངས་རྣམས་འཐོབ། །ཁམས་
གསུམ་ཡོངས་སྒྲོལ་ཏིང་འཛིན་གྱིས། །ནམ་མཁའ་ཆོས་སྐུ་ཉག་ཅིག་འཐོབ། །དཔལ་རྡོེ་གཞོན་ནུ་ཐེུཊ་ཁྲོས་པ་རྩ་བའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་བཤད་པ་ལས། སྔཊ་དྲུག་གི་ལེའུ་སྟེ་ལྔ་པའོ།། །།

༄༅། །མ་བདུད་ཐལ་བར་རློག་པའི་བྲོ། །དུར་ཁྲོད་འདི་ལ་བྲོ་བརྡུངས་པས། །དམ་ཉམས་གཤེད་ནི་བརླག་པར་འགྱུར། །ཨོཾ་རུ་ལུ་རུ་ལུ་ཧཱུྃ་བྷྱོ་ཧཱུྃ། ཕྱོགས་བཞི་རིག་ཀྱི་བྲོ་བརྡུངས་པས༑ ༑
བར་ཆད་བགེགས་ནི་སྦྱངས་པར་འགྱུར། །ཁྲོ་བཅུ་རྡོ་རྗེ་འགྲོས་ཀྱིས་བླང་། །དྲག་པོ་བྱ་ཡིས་འགྲོས་ཀྱིས་བླང་། །མཁའ་འགྲོ་ལྕེ་སྤྱང་འགྲོས་ཀྱིས་བླང་། །བདུད་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ལ་འཇུ་ཐག་གཅད། །ས་ཡི་རྟེན་
ཕུར་འོག་ཏུ་དགོད། །རྡོ་རྒྱ་གྲམ་ཐག་པས་དྲག །དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་སྟེང་དུ་དྲ་བ་བཞིན། །དུར་ཁྲོད་གཞལ་ཡས་ཁང་དུ་གཟུང་། །སྒྲུབ་པ་བྱེད་པའི་རྫས་སུ་གཟུང་། །ཐུགས་དམ་བསྐངས་པའི་བདུད་རྩིར་བཟུང་། །
ཨོཾ་རུ་ལུ་རུ་ལུ་ཧཱུཾ་བྷྱོ་ཧཱུྃ། དུར་ཁྲོད་གནས་སུ་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབས། །བསྒྲུབ་པ་ལྷ་དང་བདུད་རྩི་ལྔར། །བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་སྒྲ། །ཧཱུྃ། ཛ་ཏི་དབྱིངས་ཀྱི་ཡུམ་ཆེན་ལས། །མཁའ་འགྲོ་མང་པོའི་སྤྲུལ་
པ་འགྱེད། །ཀཽ་རི་བིན་དམར་ཞིང་བྱུག་སྔོ། །ཙི་རི་སེར་མོ་མདའ་གཞུ་འགེངས། །པྲ་མོ་ཆུ་སྲིན་རྒྱལ་མཚན་དམར་ནག་སྔོ། །པེ་ཏ་ནག་མོ་ཞིང་ཆུང་ཟ། །པུ་ཀ་དམར་སེར་རྒྱུ་ཞགས་འདྲེན། །གྷསྨ་ལྗང་ཁུ་དུང་ཁྲག་
འཐུང་། །སྨ་ཤ་མདོག་ནག་ཞིང་སྙིང་ཟ། །ཙཎྜ་སེར་སྐྱ་ཞིང་ལུག་འབྲེལ། །མ་མོ་ཆེན་པོ་ཁྱེད་བརྒྱད་ཀྱིས། །དུར་ཁྲོད་གནས་སུ་བྱིན་གྱི་ས་བརླབས། །ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ཡི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་མཛོད། །བདུད་རྩི་ལྔ་རུ་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབས། །
བྷྱོ་སེང་གདོང་སེར་མོ་རོ་བསྣོལ་ཟ། །སྟག་ག་དོང་དམར་མོ་བསྣོལ་མར་ལྟ། །ཝ་གདོང་ནག་མོ་རོ་ལ་བལྡག །ཁྱི་གདོང་མཐིང་ཁ་ཟུར་ལྟ་ལེན། །བྱ་རྒོད་གདོང་དམར་རྒྱུ་མ་འདྲེན། །ཀང་ཀ་སྔོ་སྐྱ་ཞིང་ལ་ཟ། །བྱ་

...cause them to be tormented! Seize them, strike them, bind them completely! Summon them quickly and make them speak! Having come under my power, listen to this command I give! Offer them into the mouth and absorb them into the throat; let the splendor of the body expand! <term>Vajra yaksha krodha kha tham kha tham kha. Khahi khahi khahi. Ha ha ha. Hum hum hum. Phat phat phat.</term> For the twenty-eight ritual daggers, through the two truths of the three Fathers and Mothers, they appear in the form of the Great Seal <note>original: "mahamudra"</note>. Through the gathering of <term>jati</term> and the supreme secret, the supreme son accomplishes the activities. Through the ten wrathful "Om" deities, the three poisons of the ten locations are cut from the root. Through the four gatekeepers, the four seas are dried up. Having thoroughly accomplished the Wisdom Wrathful Deity as the deity of the ritual dagger of existence, the five poisons of affliction are cut from the root. From the union of the five families of Blood-Drinkers, the accomplishment of Vajrakumara is obtained. Make the aspiration prayer for the four activities to be accomplished. All those who perform fierce acts—many weapons, garlands of weapons, syllables, sounds, fire, light, and rainbows—are employed as servants. One sees the blood-ocean, flesh, and bone-heaps of the fierce-doers everywhere, and light, smoke, and fires arise. One obtains life, increase of people, wealth, the stage of a Knowledge-Holder, and the basic space of phenomena. Through the meditative concentration that completely liberates the three realms, one obtains the single Point of the Space of the Dharma Body. From the Explanation of the Root Tantra of the Compassionate Wrath of Glorious Vajrakumara, this is the fifth chapter on the Six Mantras.

<leaf-break/>

...the dance that grinds the demons to dust. By performing the dance in this charnel ground, the killers who have violated their oaths will be destroyed. <term>Om rulu rulu hum bhyo hum</term>. By performing the dance of the four families in the four directions, the obstacles and hindering spirits will be purified. Perform the vajra-steps of the ten wrathful deities. Perform the fierce bird-steps. Perform the jackal-steps of the <term>dakinis</term>. Sever the tether at the door of the demons. Place the grounding-dagger of the earth beneath. Secure it with the cross-vajra rope. Above the mandala, like a net, hold the charnel ground celestial palace. Hold it as the substance for performing the accomplishment. Hold it as the nectar that fulfills the sacred bond. <term>Om rulu rulu hum bhyo hum</term>. Bless the charnel ground location. The sound of the qualities of blessing the deities of accomplishment and the five nectars: <term>Hum</term>! From the Great Mother of the Space of <term>Jati</term>, the emanations of many <term>dakinis</term> are sent forth. Gauri, blue-black, smears the skin of a corpse. Tsauri, yellow, draws a bow and arrow. Pramoha, with a crocodile banner, is dark red and blue. Peta, black, eats a small corpse. Pukkasi, orange-red, pulls a rope of intestines. Ghasmari, green, drinks blood from a conch. Smasha, black-colored, eats the heart of a corpse. Chandali, pale yellow, joins a corpse and a sheep. You eight Great Mothers, bless the charnel ground location! Make it the city of the Heruka! Bless it as the five nectars! <term>Bhyo</term>! Lion-headed yellow one, eat the crossed corpses! Tiger-headed red one, look at the crossed corpses! Fox-headed black one, lick the corpses! Dog-headed dark blue one, look askance and take! Vulture-headed red one, pull the intestines! Kanka-bird-headed pale blue one, eat the corpses! ...

At the tip of the nose, upon a sun and moon disk, is an indestructible <term>bindu</term> <gloss>essence drop</gloss> of white and red. My own awareness is the syllable <term>HAM</term>. From it, rays of light radiate out. I make offerings to the Three Roots and purify the sins and obscurations of all sentient beings. Gathering back, there is Guru Vajrasattva, white in color. He has one face and two hands, holding a <term>vajra</term> <gloss>scepter</gloss> and a <term>ghanta</term> <gloss>bell</gloss>. His two legs are in the cross-legged posture, adorned with the ornaments of the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>enjoyment body</gloss>. In his lap is the consort white <term>Prajna</term> <gloss>wisdom</gloss> Nyemma, free from conceptual elaborations. She holds a curved knife and a skull cup and embraces the Father in bliss. Appearance arising as bliss is Vajrasattva. Emptiness free from perceived objects is the Consort Nyemma. Within this mandala of the non-dual deity of bliss and emptiness, the Three Roots are fully complete, appearing clearly like the moon reflected in water. The light rays of the union of appearance and emptiness radiate in the ten directions. At the heart center is a <term>bindu</term>...

<leaf-break/>

...white and red, within the space of the sun and moon. In the center of a five-pointed vajra composed of the five pure essences is the syllable <term>HAM</term>, the white essence of the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body</gloss> as awareness-emptiness. From it, light radiates out from the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>expanse of reality</gloss> of self-appearance. I invite the <term>jñanasattva</term> <gloss>wisdom being</gloss> and dissolve them inseparably. Through prostrations and outer and inner offerings, may you be pleased. This is the Power of the Remedial Action. Within this, the power is perfected by making offerings to the stable forms and marks of the deity. The Power of Repentance is as follows: The nature of the mind is primordial luminosity. For the sake of beings whose vision is clouded by the thick cataract of ignorance, I pray that all obscurations, damaged commitments, and sins be removed by the surgical probe of the Bhagavan's compassion. Having thus prayed, the life-syllable at the heart...

In the <term>mandala</term> <gloss>sacred circle</gloss>, to the one possessing the essence of the hundred families of the all-pervading Lord, the Unchanging Vajra <note>original: "rdo rje"</note> <unclear>...</unclear> to reach the state of exhaustion <unclear>...</unclear> In the temple of Secret Mantra Dharma Island <note>original: "gsang sngags chos gling"</note>, the all-pervading Vajra-holder of the hundred families, Legpai Dondrub <unclear>...</unclear> to attain the supreme <term>siddhi</term> <gloss>spiritual accomplishment</gloss> <unclear>...</unclear> In the pure land of the celestial realm, to the one with immeasurable compassionate activity, Kuntuzangpo Dorje <unclear>...</unclear> may primordial wisdom arise <unclear>...</unclear> In the palace of the four joys of great bliss, the one who knows the equality of bliss, clarity, and the awareness of emptiness, Tsangse Drubpa <unclear>...</unclear> to be liberated into the body of light <unclear>...</unclear> In the palace of the unborn natural state, the one who gave birth to the <term>samadhi</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss> of immortal great bliss, the supreme accomplished Vajra <unclear>...</unclear> may the four visions arise <unclear>...</unclear> In the meditation chamber of the Oddiyana <note>referring to Guru Rinpoche</note> inner room, the one who understands the profound meaning of the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>sphere of ultimate reality</gloss>, Chokyi Nyima <unclear>...</unclear> may the two benefits <note>benefit for self and others</note> be accomplished <unclear>...</unclear> Upon the seat of the sun and moon at the crown of the head, the one who causes the rain of immortal Dharma to fall, to the Root Guru <unclear>...</unclear> grant blessings to accomplish immortality. In the place of the great light-mass of one’s own body, the celestial palace where the channels and elements gather, in the secret forest of the hidden land, you let fall a great rain of empowerments and blessings. To Tenpai Gyaltsen, I pray: grant blessings for maturation and liberation. In the fields of disciples that pervade space, to the one with immeasurable compassionate activity, the Knowledge-Holder Vajra <unclear>...</unclear> grant blessings so that self-liberation arises.

but in parts, and the material is to be mixed with a wooden rod. When the fusion is complete, they take out the matter, place it in another crucible, and melt it again. Over that molten mass, they place another portion of the powders in parts, to be united in the manner aforesaid. They melt it further, and thus they continue until all the powders are melted. If you need a <term>flux</term> <gloss>seductivo</gloss> to facilitate the fusion, you shall make it from <term>Alkali salt</term> <gloss>sale Alkali</gloss>, <term>borax</term> <gloss>borace</gloss>, and <term>black soap</term> <gloss>sapone nigro</gloss>; or from <term>D.</term> <note>possibly a specific weight or "double"</note> black soap and goldsmiths' borax. When the fusion is finished, place it for <term>cupellation</term> <gloss>cuppellandum</gloss> with a large bath of <term>lead</term> <gloss>plumbi</gloss>. If before cupellation you wish to know the increase of your gold: melt one part of your powders with three parts of pure silver, dissolve it in <term>nitric acid</term> <gloss>aqua partitionis</gloss>, and you will see the increase of the gold.

### Second Augmentation

Take three ounces of <term>iron filings</term> <gloss>martis limati</gloss>, 3 ounces of <term>copper filings</term> <gloss>veneris limate</gloss>, and nine ounces of raw and powdered <term>antimony</term> <gloss>antimoni crudi</gloss>. Mix them together, place them on the <term>cupel</term> <gloss>cinericium; an ash-hearth</gloss>, and by blowing strongly, make all the antimony fly away, so that the material remains white. Or do it this way: place the iron and copper filings into a crucible in a great fire, and when they are well-ignited, place enough <term>regulus of antimony</term> <gloss>regulo antimoni</gloss> over them so that they all melt together. Then, by placing the mass thus composed among ignited coals in a vessel, make the antimony go off in smoke, and it will consume it all. In place of filings, use <term>crocus of copper</term> <gloss>crocos veneris</gloss> and <term>crocus of iron</term> <gloss>martis</gloss> made with sulfur, afterward washed and dried. Afterward, pound the matter.
