The secret of the spirit <term>ruaḥ</term> <gloss>spirit/wind</gloss> is among the deep things, and one cannot attain it except through the path of <term>kabbalah</term> <gloss>tradition/received wisdom</gloss> and study. And know that the spirit is a vessel for all the souls, and in it the souls will connect to the body. And this is the secret of what our rabbis, of blessed memory, said: that the spirit is the connector between the soul <term>neshamah</term> <gloss>higher soul</gloss> and the body. And know that the spirit is the aspect of the intermediary between the <term>nefesh</term> <gloss>lower soul</gloss> and the <term>neshamah</term> <gloss>higher soul</gloss>.

And behold, the spirit is the aspect of the heart, and it is the dwelling place of the <term>neshamah</term> <gloss>higher soul</gloss>. And know that the spirit is the aspect of the air and it is the aspect of life. And this is the secret of what is written, "And the man became a living soul" <note>Genesis 2:7</note>. And know that the spirit is the aspect of the angel appointed over the man. And this is the secret of what our rabbis, of blessed memory, said: that for every man there is an angel appointed over him.

And know that the spirit is the aspect of the intellect and it is the aspect of understanding <term>binah</term> <gloss>understanding</gloss>. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of wisdom and understanding." And know that the spirit is the aspect of the light and it is the aspect of the radiance. And this is the secret of what is written, "And the light of the righteous shall rejoice." And know that the spirit is the aspect of holiness and it is the aspect of purity. And this is the secret of what is written, "And take not Thy holy spirit from me" <note>Psalm 51:13</note>.

And know that the spirit is the aspect of prayer and it is the aspect of supplication. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of grace and supplications" <note>Zechariah 12:10</note>. And know that the spirit is the aspect of repentance and it is the aspect of remorse. And this is the secret of what is written, "A broken spirit; a broken heart" <note>Psalm 51:19</note>. And know that the spirit is the aspect of love and it is the aspect of fear. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of the fear of the Lord."

And know that the spirit is the aspect of joy and it is the aspect of gladness. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of joy." And know that the spirit is the aspect of peace and it is the aspect of unity. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of peace." And know that the spirit is the aspect of life and it is the aspect of eternity. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of life."

And know that the spirit is the aspect of truth and it is the aspect of faith. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of truth." And know that the spirit is the aspect of grace <term>chesed</term> <gloss>loving-kindness</gloss> and it is the aspect of mercy. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of grace." And know that the spirit is the aspect of strength <term>gevurah</term> <gloss>power/severity</gloss> and it is the aspect of judgment. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of strength."

And know that the spirit is the aspect of beauty <term>tiferet</term> <gloss>beauty/harmony</gloss> and it is the aspect of truth. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of beauty." And know that the spirit is the aspect of victory <term>netzach</term> <gloss>eternity/victory</gloss> and it is the aspect of splendor <term>hod</term> <gloss>glory/splendor</gloss>. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of victory and splendor." And know that the spirit is the aspect of the foundation <term>yesod</term> <gloss>foundation</gloss> and it is the aspect of the righteous one. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of foundation." And know that the spirit is the aspect of the kingdom <term>malchut</term> <gloss>sovereignty/kingdom</gloss> and it is the aspect of the <term>shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>. And this is the secret of what is written, "And a spirit of kingdom."

վին իսկ աստուածապահ պալատանդ, յոր² սէրն Աստուծոյ լիով հանգուցեալ է, եւ շնորհք աստուածային պարգեւացն ամենեցուն իսկ յայտնի են ի վերայ ձեր: 114 Զի ահա թագաւորութիւն մեծ եւ հզօրագոյն, քան զամենայն թագաւորութիւնս, որ ոչ մարդկային ձեռամբ, այլ աստուածային աջովն է պսակեալ, զոր ոչ ոք երբէք³ կարասցէ փոխանորդել⁴, բայց միայն⁵ Քրիստոսի թագաւորութիւնն⁶: 115 Քահանայապետութիւն սուրբ եւ ճշմարիտ, լի աստուածային շնորհիւ, նախարարք եւ գալրք քրիստոսասէրք եւ բազմութիւն ամենայն ժողովրդոց՝ ժողովուրդ Քրիստոսի Աստուծոյ. եւ մեք⁷ պանծացեալ ի լոյս փառաց ձերոյ⁸ աստուածասէր թագաւորութեանդ⁹ անշարժելի հաւատով կացեալ մնացաք ի մէջ դառնաշունչ եւ դժնդակ¹⁰ եւ անաւրէն թագաւորացն Պարսից: 116 Զի յորժամ բարձին զթագաւորութիւնն, կորուսին զամենայն նախարարս¹¹ եւ զգալրս¹² աշխարհիս, կոտորեցին սրով զարս¹³ եւ զկանայս¹⁴, եւ ի գերութիւն վարեցին զբազմութիւն քաղաքաց եւ գիւղից¹⁵, իսկ¹⁶ ի մնացելոցն վերայ սուր շողացուցեալ¹⁷ բազում անգամ ջանացան դարձուցանել ի մոլորութիւն, բայց ոչ կարացին շարժել¹⁸:

117 Նաեւ¹⁹ ամաչեցին եւս անաւրէնքն²⁰ յունայնութեան իւրեանց, զի նշան քրիստոնէութեան հաւատոյ հզօրագոյն է, քան զամենայն թագաւորութիւնս հեթանոսաց. մինչեւ հրաման տալ անաւրէն թագաւորացն Կաւատայ եւ յետ նորա որդւոյ նորին Խոսրովու, թէ «Իւրաքանչիւր²¹ ոք զիւր հաւատ²² կալցի, եւ յայսմհետէ մի՛ ոք իշխեսցէ²³ նեղել զհայս. ամենեքեան մեր ծառայք են, մարմնով մեզ ծառայեսցեն. վասն հոգւոց՝ որ զհոգին դատէ՝ նա գիտէ եւ նոքա»:

118 «Ապա դարձեալ յաւուրս Խոսրովու²⁴ որդւոյ Որմզդի յետ գերութեանն Երուսաղէմի, հրաման ետ արքայն Խոսրով ժողովել²⁵ ամենայն²⁶ եպիսկոպոսաց կողմանց արեւելից եւ Ասորեստանեայց²⁷ ի դուռն արքունի. «Լսեմ, ասէ, թէ երկու²⁸ կողմանք են քրիստոնէից, եւ մին²⁹ զմիւսն նզովէ, վասնզի չհամարին իրաւացի. արդ միաբանութեամբ ամենեքեան ի մի վայր ժողովեսցին»: 119 Եւ ժողովեցան անդ ամենայն եպիսկոպոսունք³⁰ եւ երիցունք³¹ եւ ամենայն հաւատացեալք կողմանց այնոցիկ: 120 Եւ կացոյց ի վերայ նոցա ոստիկանս³² զՍմբատ³³ Բագրատունի, զանուանեալն Խոսրովնում եւ զքշկապետն արքունի: 121 էր անդ ի գերութեան եւ Զաքարիա³⁴ հայրապետն Երուսաղէմի եւ

**UNIVERSAL HISTORY**

...God-protected palace, in which the love of God is fully rested, and the grace of divine gifts is evident to all upon you. 114 For behold, yours is a great and most powerful kingdom, which is crowned not by a human hand, but by the divine right hand, which no one shall ever be able to replace except for the kingdom of Christ. 115 The priesthood is holy and true, full of divine grace; the ministers and officials are Christ-loving, and the multitude of all the people are the people of Christ God. And we, boasting in the light of the glory of your God-loving reign, have remained with an unmovable faith in the midst of the bitter, harsh, and lawless kings of the Persians. 116 For whenever they took away the kingdom, they destroyed all the ministers and officials of the land, they slaughtered men and women with the sword, and they led the multitude of cities and villages into captivity. And against those who remained, they shone the sword many times and tried to turn them into error, but they could not move them.

117 Furthermore, the lawless ones were ashamed of their vanity, because the sign of the Christian faith is more powerful than all the kingdoms of the pagans. Until the lawless kings Kavad and after him his son Khosrov gave the command: "Let everyone hold his own faith, and from now on let no one dare to trouble the Armenians. All are our servants; let them serve us with their bodies. Regarding souls, He who judges the soul knows, and they know."

118 "Then again, in the days of Khosrov, son of Hormizd, after the captivity of Jerusalem, King Khosrov gave the command to gather all the bishops of the lands of the East and Assyria to the royal court: 'I hear,' he says, 'that there are two parties of Christians, and one anathematizes the other because they do not consider them righteous. Now, let everyone gather in one place with unity.' 119 And all the bishops and priests and all the believers of those regions gathered there. 120 And he placed over them as overseer Smbat Bagratuni, the one named Khosrov-shum and the royal master of the court. 121 There was also in captivity the patriarch of Jerusalem, Zakaria, and...

they are equal, and the respective arcs facing the right angles are also equal <note>Euclid, Elements, Book 3, Proposition 26</note>. Thus, each part is one-quarter of the circle, and Wu-Ji is also one-quarter of the circle. Furthermore, the diagonal line Jia-Bing divides the angle Yi-Jia-Ding into two equal parts <note>Euclid, Elements, Book 1, Proposition 34, annotation</note>, meaning the two angles Ding-Jia-Bing and Bing-Jia-Yi are equal. The vertical angles Wu-Jia-Yin and Yin-Jia-Ji are also equal <note>Euclid, Elements, Book 1, Proposition 15</note>, and the two arcs Wu-Yin and Yin-Ji are equal. Since the arc Wu-Ji is 90 degrees, Wu-Yin must be 45 degrees. Therefore, when the sun is at Yin, the shadow must be at Bing. When the sun is below Yin, the <term>daojing</term> must be within Yi-Bing; when the sun is above Yin, the <term>zhijing</term> must be within Ding-Bing <note>All references to specific books and propositions refer to the "Elements of Geometry" (Euclid) for proof; the same applies below.</note>.

Now, from the above discussion, we explain how the two shadows convert and align with the <term>jidu</term>. For example, when the solar sphere is 45 degrees high <column-break/> and its light passes through Jia-Yi, the plumb line (<term>quxian</term>) on the <term>jidu</term> rests at Bing. When the sun is above 45 degrees, the plumb line is within the Yi-Bing side; when the sun is below 45 degrees, the plumb line is within the Ding-Bing side. Therefore, on the <term>jidu</term>, the Yi-Bing side is for <term>zhijing</term>, and the Ding-Bing side is for <term>daojing</term>.

Discussion: In the previous figure, the circular sector Jia-Wu-Ji is one-quarter of the circle. It was spoken of as a promise,
And even as the moon is left behind, it is said that the east has come.
Holding this thought, the strength of the longing, the moon that passes,
The lord speaks, and I hold it in my heart.
Thinking of the loneliness that follows,
I return to the traces, the heart that does not forget the lingering memories.
To hear such things, to be with one through the passing years,
How very sad it is, to think of the moon that fades,
The edge of the fire-starter,
The edge of the mouth.
The mysterious person who touched my heart, the strange one,
"That which is not graceful," is what he said,
The reading of this person, the confusion,
The coming of the person who is not graceful,
"Come," he said, and "Gather," he said,
Thinking only of the path of the father.
The head of the one who is known,
The hanging tassels, the love, the deep sadness,
Remaining after the play,
What is this, what is that?
The clear path of the ink, the fisherman,
Glittering,
The small gathering of the path, the haste,
I have not seen the path of the one who has left.

die Fülle des Genusses liegt bei den Ohren in der Erkennt-
niss von dem Wieviel der Zeit zwischen zwei Weisen und
den Zeiten der Ruhe und der Bewegung in denselben.

Es verhält sich ebenso mit den andern sinnlichen Wahr-
nehmungen: die Sehkraft kann das Maas irgend einer Ent-
fernung zwischen dem Erblickten nur dann erkennen, wenn
es im Raum einander nah gestellt ist; steht es zu fern, so ist's
wie wenn das Gehörte durch die Zeiten getrennt ist und kann
die Sehkraft die Distance nicht erfassen und nur noch durch
die Maasse der Geometer, Thau, Rohr, Elle, Faust, Finger
sie bestimmen. Die wahrnehmende Hörkraft kann dann die
Töne nicht mehr erfassen, nur durch Instrumente kann man
dann den Ton noch beobachten, so durch Kelche, Züngel-
chen, Kähnchen, Astrolabe und ähnliche Instrumente. Stehen
aber die Töne einander nah, so erfasst sie das Gehör und
versteht sie zu unterscheiden, wie dies bei den Versfüssen
der Fall ist. Ein anderer Grund, dass die Pause nicht zu
lang sein darf, ist, dass die Form eines Tones, wenn derselbe
zur Hörkraft gelangt, nur die Zeit von drei ihr gleichen
Griffen mit je einer Pause weilt, so dass im ganzen acht
Tempo herauskommen.

**Die Formung der Instrumente, ihre Kunst und ihre Herrichtung.**

Die Meister bildeten viel Instrumente und Geräthe für
die musikalischen Weisen und die Melodien des Gesanges.
Sie haben eine verschiedene Gestalt und sind vielartig, so
Trommel, Pauke, Rohr-Flöte, Becken, Blasinstrumente, die
Schababat (Pfeifen), die syrischen Instrumente, die Zischer,
Schilbak, Schawaschil, Laute, Cymbel, Violine, die Ma'arif,
Organa und Harmonika.

->— 117 —<-

the fullness of enjoyment for the ears lies in the knowledge of the quantity of time between two manners and the times of rest and movement within them.

It is the same with other sensory perceptions: the faculty of sight can only recognize the measure of a distance between objects if they are placed close together in space; if it is too far, it is as if the heard sound is separated by time, and the faculty of sight cannot grasp the distance and can only determine it through the measures of geometers—hair, reed, ell, fist, finger. The perceiving sense of hearing can then no longer grasp the tones; one can only observe the tone through instruments, such as cups, small tongues, small boats, astrolabes, and similar instruments. But if the tones are close to one another, the ear grasps them and understands how to distinguish them, as is the case with the feet of verses. Another reason that the pause may not be too long is that the form of a tone, when it reaches the sense of hearing, only remains for the time of three equal grips with one pause each, so that a total of eight beats result.

**The formation of the instruments, their art, and their preparation.**

The masters formed many instruments and devices for musical modes and the melodies of song. They have a different shape and are manifold, such as the drum, kettledrum, reed flute, cymbals, wind instruments, the <term>shababat</term> <gloss>pipes</gloss>, Syrian instruments, the hissers, <term>shilbak</term>, <term>shawaschil</term>, lute, cymbal, violin, the <term>ma'arif</term>, <term>organa</term>, and harmonica.

The most perfect instrument with the most beautiful effect is the instrument "lute." It has a body in which length, width, and depth stand in an exalted ratio.
Length to width = 1 : 1/2. Width to depth = 1 : 1/2.
Length to depth = 1 : 1/4. <note>82</note>
